document: Marvel Champions: The Card Game -- Rules Reference

entries.title: THE GOLDEN RULES
entries.fragment: If the text of this Rules Reference directly contradicts the text of the Learn to Play book, the text of the Rules Reference takes precedence.

entries.title: THE GRIM RULE
entries.fragment: If players are unable to find the answer to a rules or timing conflict in this Rules Reference, resolve the conflict in the manner that the players perceive as the worst possible resolution at that moment with regards to winning the scenario, and continue with the game.

entries.title: COMPONENT LIMITATIONS
entries.fragment: There is no limit to the number of threat tokens, damage tokens, acceleration tokens, status cards, or all-purpose counters that can be in the game at a given time.

entries.title: ROUND OVERVIEW
entries.fragment: The following is an overview of a game round, and the glossary entries that cover each part of the game round.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: An ability is game text on a card that explains what the card does (or can do).

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Card abilities only interact with cards that are in play, unless the ability specifically refers to an out-of-play area or element.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Card abilities on hero, alter-ego, ally, upgrade, and support cards may only be used if the card is in play, unless the ability specifically refers to being used from an out-of-play state.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: If an ability specifies one or more targets, that ability can only be initiated if it has at least one valid target.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Examples of targets include but are not limited to: “the villain,” “a minion,” “an enemy,” “a scheme,” “a hero,” “an ally,” “a character,” “a player,” “you,” “a card.”

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: When an ability has more than one sentence of text, read the entirety of the ability to check for alteration effects that may change the way the ability resolves.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: An ability prefaced by a bold timing trigger followed by a colon is referred to as a triggered ability.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Player card abilities cannot resolve during game setup, unless prefaced by a “Setup” timing trigger.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: The resolution of the following ability types is mandatory: constant abilities, “Setup” abilities, “When Revealed” abilities, “When Defeated” abilities, “Forced Action” abilities, “Forced Interrupt” abilities, “Forced Response” abilities, “Boost” abilities, and keywords.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: If one of these ability types uses the word “may”, the part of the ability following “may” is optional.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: The resolution of the following ability types is optional: “Action”, “Interrupt”, “Response”, “Resource”.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Only the player who controls a player card with an attachment that uses the word “you” or “your” can trigger abilities or pay costs on that attachment.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Only the player with an obligation in their play area can trigger abilities or pay costs on that obligation.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Some constant abilities continuously seek a specific condition (denoted by words such as “during”, “if”, or “while”).

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: If multiple instances of the same constant ability are in play, each instance affects the game independently.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: Unless prefaced by the word “Forced”, all interrupt and response abilities are optional.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: “Forced” abilities, “When Revealed” abilities, “When Defeated” abilities, and “When Completed” abilities are triggered by the game at the ability’s appropriate timing point.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: If the bold timing trigger of an ability contains the word “Hero” or “Alter-Ego,” the ability can only be used if the player triggering the ability is in the specified form.

entries.title: ABILITY
entries.fragment: If quotation marks are used around a timing trigger and colon, the quoted text is not itself a timing trigger, but is instead referring to other abilities with that trigger.

entries.title: ACCELERATION ICON
entries.fragment: An acceleration icon represents additional forces that are advancing the villain’s nefarious plans.

entries.title: ACCELERATION ICON
entries.fragment: Each acceleration icon is equivalent to the following constant ability: “During the Place Threat step of the villain phase, place 1 additional threat on the main scheme.”

entries.title: ACCELERATION ICON
entries.fragment: An acceleration icon can be removed from play by defeating the encounter card it is printed on.

entries.title: ACCELERATION ICON
entries.fragment: Accleration icons are not considered acceleration tokens, and vice versa.

entries.title: ACCELERATION TOKEN
entries.fragment: Acceleration tokens are functionally equivalent to acceleration icons (but are not considered acceleration icons).

entries.title: ACCELERATION TOKEN
entries.fragment: If the encounter deck is empty, place one acceleration token next to the main scheme.

entries.title: ACCELERATION TOKEN
entries.fragment: Card effects may instruct the players to add an acceleration token to play.

entries.title: ACCELERATION TOKEN
entries.fragment: Acceleration tokens placed on cards other than the main scheme still add threat to the main scheme during step one of the villain phase.

entries.title: ACCELERATION TOKEN
entries.fragment: Acceleration tokens placed on cards other than the main scheme are removed from play when the card they are placed on leaves play.

entries.title: ACCELERATION TOKEN
entries.fragment: Accleration tokens are not considered acceleration icons, and vice versa.

entries.title: ACTION
entries.fragment: “Action” is a type of triggered ability.

entries.title: ACTION
entries.fragment: Players can only trigger action abilities on cards they control or on encounter cards.

entries.title: ACTION
entries.fragment: Players cannot trigger action abilities on obligations in other players’ play areas.

entries.title: ACTION
entries.fragment: Each “Forced Action” ability must be resolved before the player phase can end.

entries.title: ACTION
entries.fragment: A forced action ability can be triggered at any time a non-forced action ability could be triggered.

entries.title: ACTION
entries.fragment: If such an ability has a cost that cannot be paid or requires one or more valid targets and has none, the phase can end without that ability being resolved.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: There are two types of enemy activations: an attack activation and a scheme activation.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: During step two of the villain phase, the villain activates once per player, in player order.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: During step two of the villain phase, each minion engaged with a player activates against that player.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: Each time the villain activates, give the villain one boost card from the encounter deck for that activation.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: Some card abilities can also cause enemies to attack or scheme.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: If multiple enemies activate against you simultaneously, resolve the villain’s activation first (if any) in the order of your choice, followed by minion activations in the order of your choice.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: If an activating minion leaves play, that minion’s activation ends immediately and no further steps of that activation resolve.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: An effect that initiates an enemy activation is considered resolved after that activation has fully resolved.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: If an effect initiates an activation during the resolution of another activation, the newly initiated activation resolves after the current activation has finished resolving.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: If multiple activations are initiated this way, the first player decides the order in which they are resolved.

entries.title: ACTIVATION
entries.fragment: All abilities triggered by the initial activation resolve before subsequent activations initiate.

entries.title: ACTIVE PLAYER
entries.fragment: The player taking their turn during the player phase is the active player.

entries.title: “AFTER”
entries.fragment: The word “after” refers to a game occurrence that just concluded.

entries.title: ALL-PURPOSE COUNTER
entries.fragment: All-purpose counters can be used to track a variety of different game states and statuses.

entries.title: ALL-PURPOSE COUNTER
entries.fragment: All-purpose counters are considered tokens for all game purposes.

entries.title: ALL-PURPOSE COUNTER
entries.fragment: An ability that refers to an “all-purpose counter” can refer to any all-purpose counter, regardless of what other types that counter might have.

entries.title: ALL-PURPOSE COUNTER
entries.fragment: When an all-purpose counter is moved from one card to another, it loses any previous type it had and gains the type defined on the new card it occupies.

entries.title: ALLIANCE
entries.fragment: When a player declares their intention to play a card with the alliance keyword, any player(s) may help pay the costs for that card.

entries.title: ALLIANCE
entries.fragment: The alliance keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “While paying costs for this card, any player may contribute to paying those costs.”

entries.title: ALLIANCE
entries.fragment: Only the player playing the card with the alliance keyword is considered to be resolving that card.

entries.title: ALLY
entries.fragment: Ally is a player card type that represents an identity’s friends, supporters, or companions.

entries.title: ALLY
entries.fragment: If an ally enters play, it remains in play until a card ability or game effect causes it to leave play.

entries.title: ALLY
entries.fragment: During a player’s turn, they may use any number of allies they control to attack or thwart.

entries.title: ALLY
entries.fragment: After an ally is used to attack or thwart, deal consequential damage to that ally equal to the number of consequential damage icons ([consequential-damage]) beneath the ally’s ATK or THW field.

entries.title: ALLY
entries.fragment: If a player is attacked, any player may exhaust an ally they control to defend against the attack.

entries.title: ALLY
entries.fragment: Attacks, thwarts, defenses, action abilities, and triggered abilities that resolve from allies in play under a player’s control are not considered to be performed by that player’s identity.

entries.title: ALLY LIMIT
entries.fragment: Each player is permitted to control a maximum of three allies in play at any given time.

entries.title: ALTERATION EFFECT
entries.fragment: An alteration effect modifies the resolution of an ability that precedes it.

entries.title: ALTERATION EFFECT
entries.fragment: If “this/that activation/attack/thwart” is part of a condition for an effect, it does not make that effect an alteration effect.

entries.title: AMPLIFY ICON
entries.fragment: The amplify icon represents various forces that are empowering or bolstering the villain.

entries.title: AMPLIFY ICON
entries.fragment: Each amplify icon is equivalent to the following constant ability: “Each boost card gains [boost].”

entries.title: “AND”
entries.fragment: The word “and” indicates that two or more effects within an ability resolve simultaneously.

entries.title: “AND”
entries.fragment: Individual effects connected by “and” are not dependent on each other.

entries.title: “AND”
entries.fragment: Each effect connected by “and” can be canceled or prevented independently.

entries.title: ASPECT CARD
entries.fragment: Cards in the “aspect” classification are any cards that belong to the Aggression, Justice, Leadership, and/or Protection aspects.

entries.title: ASPECT CARD
entries.fragment: When building a player deck, a player must choose one of the five aspects (Aggression, Justice, Leadership, Protection, or ‘Pool) to use for customization.

entries.title: ASPECT CARD
entries.fragment: A card’s aspect is designated by the aspect’s name printed at the bottom of the card in its deckbuilding classification area.

entries.title: ASSAULT
entries.fragment: When a character makes a basic thwart against a scheme with the assault keyword, that character uses its ATK instead of its THW.

entries.title: ASSAULT
entries.fragment: The assault keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “While a character is making a basic thwart against this scheme, that character uses its ATK instead of its THW.”

entries.title: ASSAULT
entries.fragment: If the thwarting character is an ally, it takes the consequential damage listed under its ATK instead of its THW after the thwart.

entries.title: ASSAULT
entries.fragment: Abilities that increase a character’s “basic power” can be used to increase that character’s ATK when that character thwarts a scheme with assault.

entries.title: ATTACHMENT
entries.fragment: Attachment is an encounter card type.

entries.title: ATTACHMENT
entries.fragment: If an attachment attaches to a character, it may modify that character’s ATK, SCH, and/or THW values, as indicated by the values in the associated fields on the attachment card.

entries.title: ATTACHMENT
entries.fragment: If an attachment has a “SCH/THW” modifier, it modifies the attached character’s SCH if that character is a villain or minion, and modifies the attached character’s THW if that character is a hero or ally.

entries.title: ATTACHMENT
entries.fragment: If an attachment modifies a value the attached character does not have or for which that character has a dash (–) as a value, that modifier is ignored.

entries.title: ATTACHMENT
entries.fragment: When an attachment attached to a player card uses the word “you” or “your,” it refers to the attached player card’s controller.

entries.title: ATTACHMENT
entries.fragment: Only the player who controls the card to which that attachment is attached can trigger abilities or pay costs on that attachment.

entries.title: ATTACH TO
entries.fragment: If a card uses the phrase “attach to”, it must be attached to (placed beneath and slightly overlapped by) the specified game element as it enters play.

entries.title: ATTACH TO
entries.fragment: Once a card is attached, it remains in play until either the element it is attached to leaves play, in which case the attached card is discarded, or an ability or game effect causes the attached card to leave play.

entries.title: ATTACH TO
entries.fragment: An attached card exhausts and readies independently of the game element it is attached to.

entries.title: ATTACH TO
entries.fragment: The “attach to” phrase is checked for legality when the card would be attached to a game element, but it is not checked again after it is attached.

entries.title: ATTACH TO
entries.fragment: The “attach to” phrase on a card is not resolved if another ability causes that card to attach to a specific game element.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: An attack is a type of enemy activation.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: Enemy attacks are always initiated against both a player and a character.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: Normally the attacked character is the player’s hero, but abilities can instead cause an enemy to attack a player’s alter-ego or an ally that player controls.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If a character other than the attacked character defends the attack, that character becomes the new target of that attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If a player other than the attacked player defends the attack with a character they control, that player becomes the new target of that attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: Abilities that trigger “When/After [enemy] attacks you” are resolved when/after a player is attacked, regardless of which character they control was attacked.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: The defending character becomes the target character for the attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If a player other than the target player defends, the defending player becomes the target player for the attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: The base damage is equal to the attacking enemy’s ATK, including modifiers from abilities in play and boost icons resolved for the attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If a hero has been declared the defender of the attack, reduce the amount of damage dealt by that hero’s DEF value.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If a hero was declared the defender of the attack, the damage from the attack is dealt to that hero.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: The defending hero is considered to have been attacked.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If a hero with a tough status makes a basic defense, the damage is first reduced by that hero’s DEF value.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If an ally was declared the defender of the attack, all damage from the attack is dealt to the ally.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: The defending ally is considered to have been attacked.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If the defending ally leaves play prior to damage from the attack being dealt, the attack is considered to have no character defending and the identity of that ally’s controller becomes the target of the attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If no character was declared the defender of the attack, the attack is considered undefended.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: The targeted character is considered to have been attacked.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: “after [character] attacks [and damages/defeats] [you/an ally]...”

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: “after [character] is attacked...”

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: “after [character] defends [and takes no damage]...”

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: “after [character] [takes/deals] damage...” b.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: Interrupts that trigger “when [enemy name] attacks” have the same timing as interrupts that trigger “when [the villain/an enemy] initiates an attack.”

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: If an enemy attack ends before damage is dealt, abilities that trigger after an attack or after a character defends an attack resolve as normal.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: Abilities that trigger when an enemy “attacks and damages” or “attacks and defeats” a character trigger only when that character is damaged/defeated by damage from the attack itself, and not by an ability that resolves during the attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: For example, Sonic Converter reads: “Forced Response: After Klaw attacks and damages a character, stun that character.” If Klaw is given a boost ability that says “Boost: Deal 1 damage to each hero,” that boost ability does not trigger the ability on the Sonic Converter.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: Some game effects and card abilities reference an attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: A hero or ally can use their basic attack power to attack an enemy.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: A character can only initiate a basic attack if there is an enemy that can be attacked by that character or if that character is stunned.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: An ability that allows a hero or ally to “make a basic attack without exhausting” can allow an exhausted character to make a basic attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: If a triggered ability is labeled as an attack—such as “Hero Action (attack)”—resolving that ability is considered to attack the specified target.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: An ability labeled as an attack is considered a single attack, even if that attack deals multiple instances of damage.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: When an attack ability has its damage increased by another ability, each instance of damage in that attack ability that does not use the word “additional” is increased by the specified amount.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: If an ability says “Make the following X attacks in order,” followed by two or more instances of damage, each of those instances is considered a separate attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: An ability that increases the damage of an attack only increases the damage of one of that ability’s attacks, though such an ability can be triggered separately for each attack.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: Hero and ally attacks can target any enemy, unless a card ability (such as guard) is preventing that enemy from being attacked.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: When an attack targets multiple enemies, the attacking character is considered to have attacked each of those enemies.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: Each attacked enemy with the retaliate X keyword that is still in play after the attack resolves deals its retaliate damage to the attacking character.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: The order of resolution for abilities triggered by the resolution of an attack is as follows: 7.

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: “after [character] attacks [and damages/defeats] [an enemy/a minion]...”

entries.title: ATTACK (PLAYER ABILITY TYPE)
entries.fragment: “after [character] is attacked...” 8.

entries.title: ATTACKS AGAINST ALLIES
entries.fragment: Some effects cause a villain or minion to attack an ally directly.

entries.title: ATTACKS AGAINST ALLIES
entries.fragment: The player who controls the ally is considered the attacked player.

entries.title: ATTACKS AGAINST ALLIES
entries.fragment: Abilities that resolve while/when/after the attacking enemy “attacks you” resolve against the attacked player.

entries.title: ATTACKS AGAINST ALLIES
entries.fragment: Any boost abilities that refer to “you” refer to the player who controls the attacked ally.

entries.title: ATTACKS AGAINST ALLIES
entries.fragment: Players may defend these attacks as normal by declaring a hero or an ally as the defender.

entries.title: ATTACKS AGAINST ALLIES
entries.fragment: If the attack has overkill and defeats an ally (whether that ally was the attacked ally or a defending ally), any excess damage from that attack is dealt to the identity of the player who controlled the defeated ally.

entries.title: BASE VALUE
entries.fragment: A defined value before modifiers are applied.

entries.title: BASIC CARD
entries.fragment: Cards in the “Basic” classification are cards that are not associated with a specific identity or aspect.

entries.title: BASIC CARD
entries.fragment: When building a deck, a player may customize the remainder of their deck (the portion not allocated to their identity-specific cards) using basic cards.

entries.title: BASIC CARD
entries.fragment: A card is designated as basic if it has the word “Basic” printed at the bottom of the card in its deckbuilding classification area.

entries.title: BASIC CARD
entries.fragment: Basic cards are not aspect cards.

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: A basic power is a statistic that allows a character to perform a certain game function.

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: There are five different basic powers:

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: Attack power (ATK) can be used by a character to perform a basic attack and deal damage to another character.

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: Thwart power (THW) can be used by a character to perform a basic thwart and remove threat from a scheme.

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: Defense power (DEF) can be used by a character to perform a basic defense and prevent damage from an attack.

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: Recovery power (REC) can be used by a character to perform a basic recovery and heal damage from themself.

entries.title: BASIC POWER
entries.fragment: Scheme power (SCH) can be used by a character to perform a basic scheme and place threat on the main scheme.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: Each time the villain attacks or schemes, the villain is given one facedown card from the encounter deck, as a boost card.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: A star icon is not itself considered a boost icon, and does not contribute to the villain’s ATK or SCH value.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: Only the ability text beneath the divider line is active on a card that is resolving as a boost card.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: Damage dealt by a boost ability is not considered to be damage dealt by the activation during which the boost ability resolved.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: If additional boost cards are resolved for an activation, the boost icons are cumulative, and all “Boost” abilities on those cards resolve.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: After applying a boost card to an activation, discard it.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: If an enemy is dealt a boost card outside of its own activation, that boost card remains facedown on that enemy until that enemy activates.

entries.title: BOOST, BOOST ICON
entries.fragment: If that enemy is a villain or a minion with the villainous keyword, it still gets dealt another boost card at the start of its activation as normal.

entries.title: CAMPAIGN-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: Cards in the “campaign-specific” classification are cards that belong to a campaign’s set of accompanying cards.

entries.title: CAMPAIGN-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: Campaign-specific cards can only be used during a campaign from the same product (determined by that product’s set icon).

entries.title: CAMPAIGN-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: A campaign’s rules determine how players utilize campaign-specific cards within that campaign.

entries.title: CAMPAIGN-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: A campaign-specific card is designated by the word “Campaign” printed at the bottom of the card in its encounter set name area.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: Some card abilities can cancel card or game effects.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: Cancel abilities interrupt the initiation of effects and prevent them from resolving.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: Anytime the effects of an ability are canceled, the ability (apart from its effects) is still regarded as initiated, and any costs are still paid.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: If the effects of an event card are canceled, the card is still considered played, and it is discarded.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: If the effects of a treachery card are canceled, the card is still regarded as revealed, and it is still placed in the encounter discard pile.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: Cancel effects are considered a subtype of replacement effect, with the canceled effect being replaced with no effect.

entries.title: CANCEL
entries.fragment: Abilities dependent on the canceled effect cannot trigger as the canceled effect is not considered to have occurred.

entries.title: “CANNOT”
entries.fragment: The word “cannot” is absolute and cannot be countermanded by other abilities or effects.

entries.title: “CANNOT”
entries.fragment: If two abilities conflict, the ability with “cannot” takes precedence.

entries.title: “CANNOT”
entries.fragment: If two rules conflict, the rule with “cannot” takes precedence.

entries.title: “CANNOT”
entries.fragment: An ability can override a rule with “cannot” per the Golden Rules.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: A card’s card type denotes various rules and game functions associated with that card.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: Ally, event, identity, player side scheme, resource, support, and upgrade cards are types of player cards.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: Attachment, environment, main scheme, minion, obligation, side scheme, treachery, and villain cards are types of encounter cards.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: If an ability causes a card to change its card type, it loses all other card types it might possess and functions as would any card of the new card type.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: Any cards attached to a card that changes type remain attached, but only those abilities that refer to the new card type remain active.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: An ally that has been changed to a minion engages its controller and does not take consequential damage after it attacks or schemes.

entries.title: CARD TYPES
entries.fragment: When a player changes a minion to an ally, that player takes control of that ally.

entries.title: CHARACTER
entries.fragment: Identities (heroes and alter-egos), allies, villains, and minions are all characters.

entries.title: CHOOSE (GAME ELEMENT)
entries.fragment: The phrase “choose a [game element]” (such as an ally, a minion, or a scheme) indicates that a player must select a game element that meets the specific requirements of an ability.

entries.title: CHOOSE (GAME ELEMENT)
entries.fragment: The player resolving the ability that uses the word “choose” is the player who makes the choice specified by the card.

entries.title: CHOOSE (GAME ELEMENT)
entries.fragment: If a player card ability requires the choosing of one or more targets, and there are no valid targets for any part of the ability, the ability cannot be initiated.

entries.title: CHOOSE (GAME ELEMENT)
entries.fragment: If multiple targets are required to be chosen by the same player, simultaneously choose as many as are available, to a maximum of the specified number.

entries.title: CHOOSE (GAME ELEMENT)
entries.fragment: The same target cannot be chosen multiple times this way.

entries.title: CHOOSE (GAME ELEMENT)
entries.fragment: An effect that can choose “any number” of targets does not successfully resolve if zero of those targets are chosen.

entries.title: CHOOSE (OPTION)
entries.fragment: Some abilities instruct a player to choose between multiple options.

entries.title: CHOOSE (OPTION)
entries.fragment: When an encounter card requires a player to choose an option, they cannot choose an option that requires one or more targets if there are no valid targets for that option.

entries.title: CHOOSE (OPTION)
entries.fragment: When a player card requires a player to choose an option, they cannot choose an option that cannot be at least partially resolved.

entries.title: CHOOSE (OPTION)
entries.fragment: Have a cost the player cannot pay.

entries.title: CHOOSE (OPTION)
entries.fragment: Require one or more targets and there are no valid targets.

entries.title: CHOOSE (OPTION)
entries.fragment: When a card requires a player to choose multiple options from a list, that player cannot choose the same option multiple times.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: A card’s classification is the group that a card belongs to as determined by its specific attributes.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “identity-specific” classification are cards that belong to an identity’s set of accompanying cards.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “aspect” classification are cards that belong to the Aggression, Justice, Leadership, Protection, and/or ‘Pool aspects.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “Basic” classification are not associated with a specific identity or aspect.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “scenario-specific” classification are cards that belong to a scenario’s set of accompanying cards.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “modular encounter set” or “modular set” classification are cards that belong to a modular set of encounter cards.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “campaign-specific” classification are cards that can only be used during a campaign from the same product.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “Standard” classification are cards that are added to most scenarios.

entries.title: CLASSIFICATIONS
entries.fragment: Cards in the “Expert” classification are cards that are added to scenarios when playing expert mode.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: Confuse is a status that cancels a character’s next scheme or thwart.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: A confused status card resolves like the triggered ability: “Forced Interrupt: When this character would scheme or thwart, remove each confused status card from it instead.”

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: If an ability “confuses” a character, give that character a confused status card.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: A character is confused if it has a confused status card.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: A character with the steady keyword is confused only if it has two confused status cards.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: If a character has an ability stating that it “cannot be confused,” confused status cards cannot be placed on that character.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: If a confused identity or ally attempts to thwart or use a thwart ability, discard the confused card instead.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: A confused character can attempt to thwart or use a thwart ability even if it has no valid target for a thwart.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: If a confused villain or minion would scheme, discard the confused status card instead.

entries.title: CONFUSE, CONFUSED
entries.fragment: As the thwart action or scheme activation was replaced by the removal of the confused status card, that character is not considered to have thwarted or schemed.

entries.title: CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGE
entries.fragment: After an ally attacks, it takes consequential damage equal to the number of consequential damage icons ([consequential-damage]) beneath its ATK field.

entries.title: CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Consequential damage is dealt to an ally after resolving abilities that are triggered by the ally attacking or thwarting.

entries.title: CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGE
entries.fragment: If the target of an ally’s basic power leaves play before that ally deals damage equal to its ATK or removes threat equal to its THW, the ally does not take consequential damage (but still exhausts).

entries.title: CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGE
entries.fragment: That ally is not considered to have attacked or thwarted for the purpose of other abilities.

entries.title: CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGE
entries.fragment: For example, Iron Fist’s ability reads: “Interrupt: When Iron Fist attacks an enemy, remove 1 mystic counter from him stun that enemy and deal 1 damage to it.” If this effect defeats the enemy Iron Fist was attacking, the basic attack aborts as soon as the target leaves play, so Iron Fist does not take consequential damage from it.

entries.title: COPY
entries.fragment: A copy of a card is defined by title.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: A card’s resource cost is the numerical value that must be paid to play the card.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: A cost arrow icon () in ability text distinguishes a cost from an effect, in a “pay cost resolve effect” format.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: Text indicating the timing of an interrupt or response trigger that precedes a cost arrow is not considered part of the cost.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: A resource cost with the per-player icon ([per-player]) is multiplied by the number of players who started the scenario.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If a cost with the per-player icon is reduced, the total cost of the card is reduced, not the value that is multiplied by the number of players.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: To pay a resource cost, a player spends resources that they generate by discarding cards from their hand or by using “Resource” card abilities.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: Resources generated to pay for an ability on a card are considered to have been paid for that card.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: While paying a cost, a player is permitted to generate resources beyond the specified cost.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: Resources generated beyond the specified cost are considered to have been overpaid for that cost and were not paid for that cost.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: Any resources that are generated beyond the specified cost are lost after paying that cost.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If multiple costs for a single card or ability require payment, those costs must be paid simultaneously.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: A player generating resources for those costs chooses how to divide those resources between those costs.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: An ability’s cost cannot be paid if that ability’s effect requires one or more targets and there is not at least one valid target.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: While a player is paying a cost, that player must pay costs with cards and/or game elements they control.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If a cost uses the word “choose,” the player can choose targets they do not control.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If a cost targets a “friendly” card, the player can target cards they do not control.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If a cost requires a game element that is not in play, the player paying the cost may only use game elements that are in their own out-of-play areas.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: A cost requiring “any number” or “up to” some number of game elements requires a minimum of one such game element.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: Some card abilities may reference an “additional cost.” A player must pay all additional costs simultaneously with the cost that is being added to, even if multiple cards or abilities are adding separate additional costs.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If dealing damage is a cost, that cost is considered paid even if some or all of that damage is prevented.

entries.title: COST
entries.fragment: If taking damage is a cost, that cost is not considered paid unless all of that damage was taken.

entries.title: COST ARROW ICON ()
entries.fragment: A cost arrow icon () in ability text distinguishes a cost from an effect, in a “pay cost resolve effect” format.

entries.title: COST ARROW ICON ()
entries.fragment: Responses to the text preceding the cost arrow icon resolve before the text following the icon resolves.

entries.title: CRISIS ICON
entries.fragment: While at least one crisis icon is in play, threat cannot be removed from the main scheme by player cards.

entries.title: CRISIS ICON
entries.fragment: Each crisis icon is equivalent to the following constant ability: “Player cards cannot remove threat from the main scheme.”

entries.title: CRISIS ICON
entries.fragment: Abilities on encounter cards are not affected by the crisis icon.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Damage reduces a character’s hit points.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Damage on an identity or villain is tracked by a hit point dial.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Damage on an ally or minion is tracked by damage tokens.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: When damage is dealt to a character, that character takes damage.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: When the amount of damage an effect deals is modified, the amount of damage the character takes is similarly modified.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: When the amount of damage a character takes is modified (such as by damage being prevented), the amount of damage dealt is not modified.

entries.title: DAMAGE
entries.fragment: The order of resolution for effects surrounding the dealing and taking of damage are as follows: 1.

entries.title: DASH (VALUE)
entries.fragment: A value presented as a dash (–) indicates that value cannot be used.

entries.title: DASH (VALUE)
entries.fragment: If a card has a dash (–) as its cost value, that card cannot be played and can only enter play through other means.

entries.title: DASH (VALUE)
entries.fragment: If a character’s power (ATK, DEF, REC, SCH, and THW) has a dash (–) as the value, the character cannot exhaust to use that power.

entries.title: DASH (VALUE)
entries.fragment: If a game step or card ability references a value of dash (–), that value is treated as an unmodifiable 0.

entries.title: DEAL, DEAL AN ENCOUNTER CARD
entries.fragment: During step three of the villain phase, each player is dealt one facedown encounter card.

entries.title: DEAL, DEAL AN ENCOUNTER CARD
entries.fragment: If a player is dealt an encounter card during step three or four of the villain phase, the extra encounter card is added to the queue of cards that are being dealt and revealed in those same steps.

entries.title: DECK
entries.fragment: There are four main types of decks that appear in a game: the player deck, the encounter deck, the villain deck, and the main scheme deck.

entries.title: DECK
entries.fragment: The order of cards within a deck cannot be altered unless a player is instructed to do so by a game step, game function, or card ability.

entries.title: DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If a character has zero or fewer remaining hit points, or if a side scheme has no threat on it, it is defeated.

entries.title: DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If an ally, minion, or side scheme is defeated, it is discarded.

entries.title: DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If an identity or stage of the villain is defeated, it is removed from the game.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: During an enemy attack, a player may defend against that attack using cards they control.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Only one player at a time can defend against an enemy attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: A hero can use their basic defense power to defend against an enemy attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: When a card ability says to “declare [a hero] the defender” of an attack, that hero is considered to be making a basic defense.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: A card ability that allows a hero to be declared as a defender without exhausting can be used on an exhausted hero.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: An ally can exhaust to defend against an enemy attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: When an ally defends an attack, that ally becomes the target character for that attack, and its controller becomes the target player for that attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: When a card ability says to “declare [an ally] the defender” of an attack, that ally becomes the defender of the attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: A card ability that allows an ally to be declared as a defender without exhausting can be used on an exhausted ally.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: When a player initiates a triggered ability labeled as a defense—such as “Hero Interrupt (defense)”— during an enemy attack, that player’s identity becomes the defender and is considered to have defended the attack if there is not already a defender.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: The player’s identity is considered to be the defender as soon as the defense-labeled ability begins resolving.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Abilities that trigger “when your hero defends against an attack” can be triggered when resolving a defense-labeled ability.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Resolving a defense-labeled ability is not a basic defense and does not cause a hero to reduce the amount of damage dealt by that hero’s DEF.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Unless specified by the ability’s text, a hero does not exhaust when using a defense-labeled ability.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: The defending player may resolve any number of defense abilities during an enemy attack (as long as the triggering conditions of those abilities are met).

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Once a player resolves a defense-labeled ability during an enemy attack, other players cannot resolve defense-labeled abilities for that same attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Defense-labeled abilities can be played during an attack by a player whose ally is defending that attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: A player can trigger abilities labeled as a defense outside of an attack if the ability’s triggering condition is met.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: If a player defends against an enemy attack that targets a different player (either by defending with a character they control or by resolving a defense ability), the defending player becomes the new target of that attack.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Any triggered ability that refers to “you” refers to the player who was the target of the attack when that ability resolved.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Any constant or boost abilities that refer to “you” refer to the defending player.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: If no character is used to defend against an enemy attack, that attack is considered undefended.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: Abilities that trigger after a character defends an attack resolve after that attack ends.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: If an effect causes a defended attack to end before fully resolving, the attack is still considered to have been defended.

entries.title: DEFEND, DEFENSE
entries.fragment: If an ability triggers after a character uses a basic power, that ability triggers after an attack in which a character made a basic defense resolves.

entries.title: DELAYED EFFECT
entries.fragment: Some abilities contain delayed effects.

entries.title: DELAYED EFFECT
entries.fragment: Delayed effects resolve automatically and immediately after their specified timing point or future condition occurs or becomes true, and before responses to that point or condition may be used.

entries.title: DELAYED EFFECT
entries.fragment: Delayed effects have the same timing priority as constant effects.

entries.title: DELAYED EFFECT
entries.fragment: When a delayed effect resolves, it is not treated as a new triggered ability, even if the delayed effect was originally created by a triggered ability.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: Discarding is the act of attempting to move a card from a non-discard-pile play area to a discard pile.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: If a player card is discarded, it is placed faceup on top of the owning player’s discard pile.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: If an encounter card is discarded, it is placed faceup on top of the encounter discard pile.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: If multiple cards are discarded from a player’s hand or from play by a singular effect, place those cards in the appropriate discard pile in any order.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: If multiple cards are discarded from a deck by a singular effect, place those cards in the appropriate discard pile one at a time (without changing the order).

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: These discards are considered simultaneous.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: Responses to the discarding of any of those cards are resolved after all discards are made.

entries.title: DISCARD
entries.fragment: If a player looks at a number of cards from the top of a deck and discards one or more of those cards, those cards are considered to have been discarded from the top of that deck.

entries.title: DISCARD PILE
entries.fragment: A discard pile is an out-of-play area that contains cards that have been discarded throughout the game.

entries.title: DISCARD PILE
entries.fragment: Each player has their own discard pile, and the encounter deck has its own discard pile.

entries.title: DISCARD PILE
entries.fragment: Each discard pile is open information, and may be looked at by any player at any time.

entries.title: DISCARD PILE
entries.fragment: The order of cards in a discard pile may not be changed unless a player is instructed to do so by a card ability.

entries.title: DISCARD PILE
entries.fragment: Any ability that would shuffle a discard pile of zero cards back into a deck does not shuffle the deck.

entries.title: DOUBLE-SIDED CARD
entries.fragment: A card is double-sided if neither of its sides has a card back (player, villain, or encounter).

entries.title: DOUBLE-SIDED CARD
entries.fragment: When a double-sided card would enter an out-of-play area other than the victory display or set-aside area, it is removed from the game.

entries.title: DOUBLE-SIDED CARD
entries.fragment: If a double-sided card has “Standard Mode Only” and “Expert Mode Only” sides, it is put into play with the “Expert Mode Only” side faceup if the players are playing expert mode.

entries.title: DRAW, DRAWING CARDS
entries.fragment: If a player is instructed to draw one or more cards, those cards are drawn from the top of their deck one at a time.

entries.title: DRAW, DRAWING CARDS
entries.fragment: Drawn cards are added to a player’s hand.

entries.title: DRAW, DRAWING CARDS
entries.fragment: Each player’s hand size is checked at the end of the player phase.

entries.title: “EACH PLAYER”
entries.fragment: When each player is instructed to resolve an effect, each player resolves that effect one at a time.

entries.title: “EACH PLAYER”
entries.fragment: If the effect does not specify what order the players resolve the effect in, the first player decides the order.

entries.title: “EACH PLAYER”
entries.fragment: If a player cannot fully resolve that effect, they resolve it as fully as possible.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER CARD
entries.fragment: There are eight encounter card types: attachment cards, environment cards, minion cards, main scheme cards, obligation cards, side scheme cards, treachery cards, and villain cards.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER CARD
entries.fragment: Encounter cards belong to various classifications, such as scenario-specific encounter cards or modular set encounter cards.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER CARD
entries.fragment: Most encounter cards have an orange card back.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER DECK
entries.fragment: The encounter deck contains the encounter cards (attachments, environments, minions, side schemes, and treacheries) that players can face during a scenario.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER DECK
entries.fragment: The order of cards within the encounter deck cannot be changed unless a player is instructed to do so by a game step, game function, or card ability.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER DECK
entries.fragment: If a card ability discards a specified number of cards from the encounter deck or until a card with specific criteria is discarded, discard cards from the encounter deck until the discard condition is met or the encounter deck is empty.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER DECK
entries.fragment: If the encounter deck empties during the resolution of any other type of game effect (for example, the dealing of encounter cards), that effect finishes resolving after the encounter deck has been reset.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER DECK
entries.fragment: If there are no cards in both the encounter deck and the encounter discard pile simultaneously (such as all cards from the encounter deck being in play), an infinite loop occurs with an infinite number of acceleration tokens being placed next to the main scheme deck.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: An encounter set is a grouping of encounter cards.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: There are four types of encounter sets: scenario- specific encounter sets, modular encounter sets, the Standard set, and the Expert set.

entries.title: ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: Encounter sets with the same name but different set icons are considered distinct sets.

entries.title: END OF PLAYER PHASE
entries.fragment: To end the player phase, perform the following steps: 1.

entries.title: ENEMY
entries.fragment: An enemy is a minion or villain.

entries.title: ENERGY RESOURCE
entries.fragment: An energy resource ([energy]) is one of the four types of resources.

entries.title: ENERGY RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Energy resources can be spent to pay the resource cost of cards and abilities.

entries.title: ENERGY RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Some card abilities specifically require energy resources to be spent in order to resolve their effects.

entries.title: ENGAGE
entries.fragment: When a minion enters play in a player’s play area, it engages that player.

entries.title: ENGAGE
entries.fragment: An engaged minion remains engaged with the same player until it is defeated, removed from play, or a card ability causes it to engage another player.

entries.title: ENGAGE
entries.fragment: If a card ability instructs a player to engage a minion, that minion is also considered to have engaged that player.

entries.title: ENGAGE
entries.fragment: While a minion is engaged with a player, card abilities cannot cause the minion to engage with the same player again (as the two are already engaged).

entries.title: ENTERS PLAY
entries.fragment: The phrase “enters play” refers to any time when a card transitions from an out-of-play area into play.

entries.title: ENVIRONMENT
entries.fragment: Environment is an encounter card type that creates an overarching rule or set of rules for the scenario.

entries.title: ENVIRONMENT
entries.fragment: If an environment enters play, it remains in play until a card ability or game effect causes it to leave play.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: Event is a player card type that is generally played for an instantaneous effect.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: If an event has more than one triggered ability on it, the player playing it chooses one of those abilities to trigger when playing that event.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: If the effects of an event are canceled, the card is still considered to have been played, and its costs remain paid.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: An event card cannot be played if it requires one or more targets and does not have at least one valid target.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: Event cards are considered to be an extension of an identity.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: If an effect modifies the amount of damage an event deals or the amount of threat an event removes, and that event deals multiple instances of damage or removes multiple instances of threat, each of those instances is modified.

entries.title: EVENT
entries.fragment: If an effect modifies the amount of damage “an attack” deals (rather than “an event”), and an event initiates multiple attacks, only the first of those attacks has its damage modified.

entries.title: EXCESS DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Excess damage is any amount of damage that is dealt to a character beyond that character’s remaining hit points.

entries.title: EXHAUSTED
entries.fragment: If a card is exhausted, it is rotated 90 degrees.

entries.title: EXHAUSTED
entries.fragment: An exhausted card cannot be exhausted again until it is ready.

entries.title: EXHAUSTED
entries.fragment: A card ability on an exhausted card is active and can still interact with the game state.

entries.title: EXPERT SET
entries.fragment: The expert set is an encounter set that is added to scenarios during expert mode.

entries.title: EXPERT SET
entries.fragment: The expert set is not a modular encounter set and cannot be selected (by the players or randomly) when a scenario requires players to choose a modular encounter set to include in that scenario.

entries.title: EXPERT SET
entries.fragment: Cards in the “Expert” classification are any cards that have the word “Expert” printed by the bottom of the card in its encounter set name area.

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: When instructed to find a card, a player searches each game area where that card could be found (play area, set-aside area, player deck, discard pile, encounter deck, etc.).

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: Players should not unnecessarily search game areas if they know where the card they are looking for can be found.

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: All game areas are subject to search when resolving a “find” instruction, with the following exceptions:

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: Facedown encounter cards in any in-play game area (whether that card is in play itself).

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: The victory display.

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: Cards that have been removed from the game.

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: If a player is instructed to “find and reveal” a minion that is already in play, that player engages that minion and resolves any keywords and/or triggered abilities that resolve as a result of that minion being revealed (such as that minion’s “When Revealed” ability).

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: That minion retains all attached cards and tokens on it.

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: That minion is not considered to be entering play.

entries.title: FIND
entries.fragment: That minion is considered to engage that player unless it was already engaged with that player.

entries.title: FIRST PLAYER
entries.fragment: A first player is determined by the players at the beginning of the game.

entries.title: FIRST PLAYER
entries.fragment: If an encounter card targets a specific player or card, and there are multiple eligible targets, the first player selects among the eligible options.

entries.title: FIRST PLAYER
entries.fragment: If an encounter card requires a card ability to be resolved, a game function to be performed, or a choice to be made but does not specify which player should act, the first player does so.

entries.title: FIRST PLAYER
entries.fragment: If two or more effects would resolve simultaneously, the first player decides the order in which to resolve them.

entries.title: FIRST PLAYER
entries.fragment: The first player has the first opportunity to use an interrupt at each appropriate game moment.

entries.title: FIRST PLAYER
entries.fragment: The first player has the first opportunity to use a response at each appropriate game moment.

entries.title: FLIP
entries.fragment: When instructed to flip a card, turn that card upside down so that the face that was faceup is now facedown.

entries.title: FLIP
entries.fragment: A foldable, “three-sided” card is considered to have flipped any time the faceup side of the card changes.

entries.title: FLIP
entries.fragment: When a card flips, if the new faceup side of that card has:

entries.title: FLIP
entries.fragment: The same card type as the previous face, the card retains all attached cards, tucked cards, status cards, and tokens.

entries.title: FLIP
entries.fragment: A different card type from the previous face, all attached cards, tucked cards, status cards, and tokens are discarded from the card.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: “For each” indicates an effect is repeated based on the number of a countable game element.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: If an effect with “for each” requires a target, that effect applies to a single target unless the “for each” clause includes a “choose” instruction.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: For example, an effect that reads “For each treachery looked at this way, remove 1 threat from a scheme” removes threat from a single scheme.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: If a “for each” effect without a “choose” instruction deals damage or removes threat, it is considered a single instance of damage dealt or threat removed, respectively.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: If a “for each” effect has a “choose” instruction, each iteration of that choice is considered a separate instance of that effect, even if the same target is chosen multiple times.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: The game state updates after each instance (for example, if a minion or side scheme is defeated).

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: Responses can be triggered after each instance.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: For example, if a player is engaged with a guard minion and uses an effect that says “for each resource you spent this way, choose an enemy and deal 2 damage to it,” that player can defeat the guard minion with one instance of 2 damage, making the villain a valid target for further instances.

entries.title: “FOR EACH”
entries.fragment: If another ability modifies a “for each” effect, that modifier is applied to each instance of the “for each” effect.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: Forced is a bold trigger word.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: “Forced Interrupt” and “Forced Response” abilities must be resolved when their triggering conditions are met.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: “Forced Action” abilities can be triggered at any time during the player phase when a non-forced action ability could be triggered, but must be resolved before the player phase can end.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: If a forced ability requires one or more targets to resolve and it has no valid targets, it does not initiate.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: Any costs that would have been paid to initiate the ability are not paid.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: For any given triggering condition, forced interrupts take priority and initiate before non-forced interrupts, and forced responses take priority and initiate before non-forced responses.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: If two or more forced abilities would initiate at the same moment, the first player determines the order in which the abilities initiate, regardless of who controls the cards bearing those abilities.

entries.title: FORCED
entries.fragment: Each forced ability must resolve as completely as possible before the next forced ability being triggered by the same triggering condition may initiate.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: A player can be in either hero or alter-ego form at a given time.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: Once each round, during their turn, each player is permitted to change form by flipping their identity card.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: When a player changes form, only the form changes.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: If a card ability causes a player to change forms, it does not count against the one voluntary form change the player is permitted during their turn that round.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: While a player is in hero form, card abilities that interact with their alter-ego do not interact with their identity.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: While a player is in alter-ego form, card abilities that interact with their hero do not interact with their identity.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: Cards with the “[type] form” keyword grant an identity unique forms.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: These forms are in addition to the identity’s alter- ego and hero forms, and they come with their own conditions for changing into them.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: When an identity changes their additional form, it does not count against the once-per-turn limit on flipping from hero to alter-ego (or vice versa), but it does count as changing form for the purpose of triggering card effects.

entries.title: FORM, CHANGE FORM
entries.fragment: Cards with the text “[type] form only” can only be played or put into play by a player whose identity is in the specified form.

entries.title: “FRIENDLY”
entries.fragment: Friendly is a blanket term that refers to cards the players control.

entries.title: “GAINS”
entries.fragment: If a card gains a characteristic (such as a trait, keyword, or ability text), the card functions as if it possesses the gained characteristic.

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: A game element is a component or person involved in playing a game of Marvel Champions.

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Cards

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Decks

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Discard Piles

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Hands (of cards)

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Hit Point Dials

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Players

entries.title: GAME ELEMENT
entries.fragment: Tokens

entries.title: GUARD
entries.fragment: While a minion with the guard keyword is engaged with a player, that player cannot use cards they control to attack a villain without this keyword.

entries.title: GUARD
entries.fragment: The guard keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “The engaged player cannot attack any villain.”

entries.title: HAND SIZE
entries.fragment: Each player checks their hand size at the end of the player phase, either discarding down to or drawing up to the number of cards indicated by their hand size value.

entries.title: HAND SIZE
entries.fragment: When drawing up to their hand size, a player draws cards one at a time, checking after each card is drawn whether they are at their hand size.

entries.title: HAZARD ICON
entries.fragment: During the Deal Encounter Cards step of the villain phase, for each hazard icon on cards in play, deal one player one additional card (not one card per player).

entries.title: HAZARD ICON
entries.fragment: Each hazard icon is equivalent to the following constant ability: “During the Deal Encounter Cards step of the villain phase, deal 1 additional encounter card.

entries.title: HEAL
entries.fragment: If an ability heals a character, damage the character has sustained can be removed from the character.

entries.title: HEAL
entries.fragment: A heal effect can only bring a character to its maximum hit points, unless the effect explicitly states it can bring the character above its maximum.

entries.title: HEAL
entries.fragment: Effects that move damage off of a character are considered to heal that character.

entries.title: HINDER X
entries.fragment: A card with the hinder X keyword enters play with X threat on it.

entries.title: HINDER X
entries.fragment: The hinder X keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “This card enters play with X threat on it.”

entries.title: HINDER X
entries.fragment: This threat is in addition to any threat it normally enters play with, such as a side scheme’s starting threat.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: Each character (identity, ally, minion, and villain) has a hit point value.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: The phrase “starting hit points” refers to an identity’s printed hit point value.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: An identity’s or villain’s hit point dial represents their remaining hit points.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: If a player’s hit point dial is reduced to zero, that player is defeated and eliminated from the game.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: If a villain’s hit point dial is reduced to zero, that stage of the villain is defeated.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: When an ability that says an identity or villain “gets +X hit points” goes into effect, increase that character’s hit point dial by X.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: If an ally or minion is damaged, track the damage by placing damage tokens on that character.

entries.title: HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: If an ability that says an ally or minion “gets +X hit points” ceases to be in effect and causes that ally or minion to have damage on it equal to or greater than its hit points, that ally or minion is defeated.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Icons are graphical elements that represent various functions within the game.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Energy Icon ([energy]): An energy icon is a resource icon that generates one energy resource when spent.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Mental Icon ([mental]): A mental icon is a resource icon that generates one mental resource when spent.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Physical Icon ([physical]): A physical icon is a resource icon that generates one physical resource when spent.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Wild Icon ([wild]): A wild icon is a resource icon that can generate one energy, mental, physical, or wild resource when spent.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Acceleration Icon ([acceleration]): An acceleration icon places additional threat on the main scheme during the villain phase.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Amplify Icon ([amplify]): An amplify icon increases the number of boost icons on boost cards during enemy activations by one.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Crisis Icon ([crisis]): A crisis icon prevents players from removing threat from the main scheme.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Hazard Icon ([hazard]): A hazard icon increases the number of encounter cards that are dealt to players during the villain phase.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Boost Icon ([boost]): A boost icon increases the activating enemy’s ATK or SCH value during enemy activations.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Star Icon ([star]): A star icon is used in conjunction with a card’s stat or boost field to indicate that there is a mandatory ability in the text box that corresponds to that field.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Consequential Damage Icon ([consequential-damage]): A consequential damage icon is used in conjunction with an ally’s ATK field or THW field.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Cost Arrow (): A cost arrow separates an ability’s cost from its effects.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Per Player Icon ([per-player]): A per player icon next to a value multiplies that value by the number of players who started the scenario.

entries.title: ICONS
entries.fragment: Unique Icon ([unique]): A unique icon in a card’s title indicates the card is unique.

entries.title: IDENTITY
entries.fragment: Identity is a player card type that represents which character a player is playing in the game.

entries.title: IDENTITY
entries.fragment: Each player begins the game in alter-ego form.

entries.title: IDENTITY
entries.fragment: If a card refers to a hero or alter-ego by title, it refers only to the identity with that title, and not to the other side of the card.

entries.title: IDENTITY
entries.fragment: Identity cards cannot be discarded from play.

entries.title: IDENTITY
entries.fragment: The faceup side of an identity card is considered to be in play.

entries.title: IDENTITY-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: Cards in the “identity-specific” classification (also sometimes called “hero-specific”) are cards that belong to an identity’s set of accompanying cards.

entries.title: IDENTITY-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: A player’s deck must include each identity-specific card associated with their chosen identity card.

entries.title: IDENTITY-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: Identity-specific cards (along with obligation cards and nemesis encounter set cards) may only be used alongside an identity if those cards share a set icon with that identity.

entries.title: IDENTITY-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: An identity-specific card is designated by the identity icon printed in the bottom right corner of the card.

entries.title: IDENTITY-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: Identity cards are identity-specific cards.

entries.title: IGNORE
entries.fragment: An ability that ignores some ability, icon, or cost treats that ability, icon, or cost as not being in effect or present while that ability is resolving.

entries.title: IGNORE
entries.fragment: When a card is played “ignoring its resource cost,” no resources are paid for that card.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: A card is considered to either be in play or out of play depending on its state within the game.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: For player cards, the faceup side of a player’s identity card is in play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: For encounter cards, the faceup side of the top card of the villain deck and the faceup side of the top card of the main scheme deck are in play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: A card enters play when it moves from an out-of-play area to a play area.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Card abilities only interact with, and can only target, cards that are in play (unless the ability text specifically refers to an out-of-play area).

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Card abilities on all card types, except event cards and treachery cards, can only be initiated or affect the game while they are in play unless they specifically refer to being used from an out-of-play area.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: If a card is double-sided (having game text on each side of the card), the faceup side of the card is in play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Event cards and treachery cards implicitly resolve from an out-of-play area, by virtue of the rules pertaining to those card types.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Cards in a player’s hand, deck, and discard pile are out of play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Cards in the encounter deck, encounter discard pile, unrevealed cards in the villain deck, unrevealed cards in the main scheme deck, and facedown encounter cards dealt to a player are out of play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Facedown cards attached to in-play cards are out of play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Any cards that have been removed from the game or that have been set aside are out of play.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: A card leaves play when it moves from a play area to an out-of-play area.

entries.title: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
path: IN PLAY AND OUT OF PLAY
entries.fragment: If a card is double-sided (having game text on each side of the card), the facedown side is out of play.

entries.title: IN PLAYER ORDER
entries.fragment: If players are instructed to perform a sequence “in player order,” the first player performs their part of the sequence first, followed by the other players in clockwise order.

entries.title: IN PLAYER ORDER
entries.fragment: If a sequence performed in player order does not conclude after each player has performed their part of the sequence once, the sequence of opportunities continues in a clockwise manner until it is complete.

entries.title: IN PLAYER ORDER
entries.fragment: The phrase “next player” always refers to the next (clockwise) player in player order.

entries.title: INCITE X
entries.fragment: When a card with the incite X keyword is revealed, place X threat on the main scheme.

entries.title: INCITE X
entries.fragment: The incite X keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “When Revealed: Place X threat on the main scheme.”

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Some card abilities may deal “indirect damage.”

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Indirect damage dealt to a player can be divided as that player chooses among characters under their control.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Indirect damage dealt to a group of players (or among players) can be divided as the group chooses among friendly characters in play.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: All indirect damage from a single source is first assigned and then resolved simultaneously.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: While assigning indirect damage, a character cannot be assigned more indirect damage than would cause it to be defeated.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: A character with a tough status card can be assigned indirect damage up to its remaining hit points, and all damage assigned to it is prevented by its tough status card.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Characters that cannot take damage cannot be assigned indirect damage.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: If indirect damage dealt to a player cannot be assigned to any character that player controls, that damage is ignored.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: If an enemy’s attack deals indirect damage, the indirect damage is dealt during step four of the enemy activation (after player’s have the opportunity to defend against the attack).

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Only the defending character, or the attacked player’s identity if the attack was undefended, is considered to have been attacked, even if other characters were assigned some or all of the indirect damage.

entries.title: INDIRECT DAMAGE
entries.fragment: For example, if you take 5 indirect damage, but you control an ally with 4 hit points remaining, you may assign 4 of that indirect damage to the ally, then assign the remaining 1 indirect damage to your identity.

entries.title: INITIATING ABILITIES
entries.fragment: When a player wishes to play a card or initiate a triggered ability, that player first declares their intent.

entries.title: INITIATING ABILITIES
entries.fragment: If any of the above steps would make the triggering condition of an interrupt ability true, that ability may be initiated just before that triggering condition becomes true.

entries.title: INITIATING ABILITIES
