entries.fragment: If any of the above steps would make the triggering condition of a response ability true, that ability may be initiated immediately after that triggering condition becomes true.

entries.title: INITIATING ABILITIES
entries.fragment: If the ability being initiated is on a card that is in play, the sequence does not stop from completing if that card leaves play during this sequence unless the card leaving play prevents a required cost from being paid.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: An interrupt ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “Interrupt” timing trigger.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: Players can only trigger interrupt abilities on cards they control or on encounter cards.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: Players cannot trigger interrupt abilities on obligations in other players’ play areas.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: Multiple interrupts may be triggered by the same triggering condition, but each interrupt can only be triggered once per occurrence of the triggering condition.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: Multiple copies of a card with an interrupt can each be triggered by the same triggering condition.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: An interrupt ability is resolved when its triggering condition initiates, but before that triggering condition resolves.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: Interrupts that use the word “would” resolve before its triggering condition initiates, when that condition becomes imminent.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: If an interrupt changes (via a replacement effect) or cancels an imminent triggering condition, further interrupts to the original triggering condition cannot be triggered.

entries.title: INTERRUPT
entries.fragment: Once all players decide they do not wish to resolve any (further) interrupts to a triggering condition, (further) interrupts to that instance of that triggering condition cannot be used.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: A keyword is an attribute that conveys specific rules to its card.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: If a card gains multiple instances of a keyword, any additional instances have no effect unless that keyword is followed by a number (e.g.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Alliance: When a player declares their intention to play an alliance card, any player(s) may help pay the costs for that card.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Assault: When a character makes a basic thwart against a scheme with the assault keyword, that character uses its ATK instead of its THW.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Form: A card with the form keyword grants an identity a unique form.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Guard: While a minion with guard is engaged with a player, that player cannot attack the villain.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Hinder X: A card with the hinder X keyword enters play with X threat on it.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Incite X: When a player reveals a card with incite X, that player places X threat on the main scheme.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Linked (Card Title): Cards with the linked keyword are set aside until the card named in parentheses brings the linked card into the game.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Overkill: Excess damage from attacks with overkill are dealt to the identity or villain.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Patrol: While a minion with patrol is engaged with a player, that player cannot thwart the main scheme.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Peril: While a player is resolving a card with peril, other players cannot help that player.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Permanent: Cards with permanent cannot leave play.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Piercing: Attacks with piercing discard tough status cards from the attacked character before damage is dealt.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Quickstrike: After this enemy engages a player, it immediately attacks that player if they are in hero form.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Ranged: Attacks with ranged ignore retaliate.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Requirement (Resources): A card with the requirement keyword cannot be played unless each resource of the specified type is spent while paying for that card’s cost.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Restricted: A player cannot control more than two restricted cards at a given time.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Retaliate X: After a character with retaliate X is attacked, deal X damage to the attacker.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Setup: Cards with setup start the game in play.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Stalwart: Characters with Stalwart cannot be stunned or confused.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Steady: A character with the steady keyword is not stunned or confused unless it has two stunned or confused status cards, respectively.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Surge: After a player reveals a card with surge, that player reveals an additional encounter card.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Team-Up: Cards with team-up cannot be played unless both characters listed by the keyword are in play.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Teamwork (): After a minion with teamwork enters play and engages a player, if there is at least one other minion that shares the specified trait in play, the minion that just entered play activates against the player it is engaged with.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Temporary: A card with temporary must be discarded from play at the end of the round.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Toughness: When a character with toughness enters play, place a tough status card on it.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Uses (X “type”): When a card with uses enters play, place X all-purpose counters from the token pool on that card.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Victory X: When a card with victory X is defeated, add it to the victory display.

entries.title: KEYWORDS
entries.fragment: Villainous: When a minion with villainous activates, give it a boost card.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: A labeled ability is a triggered ability with a parenthetical following its bold trigger text that designates that ability as an attack, defense, and/or thwart.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: The identity of the player using the labeled ability is considered to be performing the labeled effect when the labeled ability begins resolving (after costs have been paid).

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: When a player resolves an ability labeled “(attack),” that ability is considered to be an attack made by that player’s identity.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: When a player resolves an ability labeled “(defense),” that ability is considered to be a defense made by that player’s identity.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: When such an ability is initiated during an attack, the player’s identity becomes the defender of that attack.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: When a player resolves an ability labeled “(thwart),” that ability is considered to be a thwart made by that player’s identity.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: When a player resolves an ability with multiple labels, that ability is considered to be each of the labeled ability types, all made by that player’s identity.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: If a player triggers a labeled ability while their identity has one or more status cards that cancel any of the labeled ability types, the entire ability (except for its costs) is canceled.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: That identity is not considered to have attacked, defended, or thwarted.

entries.title: LABELED ABILITY
entries.fragment: Each status card on the player’s identity that cancels any of the labeled ability’s types is removed when that ability is canceled.

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: Some card abilities create effects or conditions that affect the game for a specified duration (such as “until the end of the phase” or “until the end of this attack”).

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: A lasting effect persists beyond the resolution of the ability that created it, for the duration specified by the effect.

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: For the specified duration of a lasting effect, it is treated as if it was a constant ability and has the same timing priority as a constant ability.

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: Lasting effects update whenever the game state updates.

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: If a card enters play (or changes status to meet the criteria of a specified set of affected cards) after the creation of a lasting effect, it is still affected by that lasting effect.

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: A lasting effect expires as soon as the timing point specified by its duration is reached.

entries.title: LASTING EFFECTS
entries.fragment: A lasting effect that expires at the end of a specified time period can only be initiated during that time period.

entries.title: LEADER
entries.fragment: The leader card type follows the same rules as the villain card type for all purposes.

entries.title: LEAVES PLAY
entries.fragment: The phrase “leaves play” refers to any time when a card transitions from an in-play area to an out-of-play area.

entries.title: LEAVES PLAY
entries.fragment: When a card leaves play, there is no memory of its previous state and it is considered to be a new copy of the card.

entries.title: LEAVES PLAY
entries.fragment: When a non-villain card leaves play:

entries.title: LEAVES PLAY
entries.fragment: Discard each card attached to or tucked under that card.

entries.title: LEAVES PLAY
entries.fragment: Discard each boost card given to that card.

entries.title: LEAVES PLAY
entries.fragment: Return each token and status card on that card to the supply.

entries.title: LIMIT
entries.fragment: “Limit X per [period]” is a limit that appears on some player cards.

entries.title: LIMIT
entries.fragment: If an effect with a limit is canceled, the card is still considered to have been played or the ability initiated, and it counts toward the limit.

entries.title: LINKED (CARD TITLE)
entries.fragment: Cards with the linked keyword cannot be included in any deck.

entries.title: LINKED (CARD TITLE)
entries.fragment: The linked (card title) keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “Set this card aside during setup.

entries.title: LINKED (CARD TITLE)
entries.fragment: Linked cards do not count toward the minimum or maximum deck size.

entries.title: LINKED (CARD TITLE)
entries.fragment: The number of linked cards set aside during setup is equal to the number of those cards included in the product from which the linked card came.

entries.title: LINKED (CARD TITLE)
entries.fragment: If multiple decks contain the same card named on one or more linked cards, set aside the appropriate number of cards for each deck that contains the named card.

entries.title: LINKED (CARD TITLE)
entries.fragment: When a player takes control of a card with the linked keyword, that player becomes the owner of that card.

entries.title: LOOK, LOOKED-AT
entries.fragment: If an ability instructs a player to look at cards that are otherwise hidden from the players, only the player who is resolving the ability can look at those cards.

entries.title: LOOK, LOOKED-AT
entries.fragment: While a player is looking at cards in a deck, those cards are still considered part of that deck.

entries.title: LOOK, LOOKED-AT
entries.fragment: After looking at cards in a deck, those cards are returned to that deck in the same order.

entries.title: “LOSES”
entries.fragment: If a card loses a characteristic (such as a trait, keyword, or ability text), the card functions as if it does not possess the gained characteristic.

entries.title: “LOSES”
entries.fragment: Lost characteristics are still considered to be printed on the card.

entries.title: “LOSES”
entries.fragment: A lost characteristic cannot be regained while the ability causing it to be lost is in effect, even if a new effect would cause the characteristic to be gained.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: Main scheme is an encounter card type.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: During step one of the villain phase, place the amount of threat indicated in the main scheme’s acceleration field (bottom-right corner) on that scheme.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: If the amount of threat on a main scheme is equal to or greater than its target threat value, that main scheme is completed and the main scheme deck advances.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: If the villain completes the final stage of the main scheme deck, the villain wins the game.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: If the main scheme advances other than through having threat on it equal to or greater than its target threat value, that main scheme is not considered completed.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: When the main scheme deck advances, follow these steps: 1.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: When the main scheme deck advances, excess threat from the previous stage does not carry over to the new stage.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: When the main scheme deck advances, acceleration tokens on it carry over to the new stage.

entries.title: MAIN SCHEME, MAIN SCHEME DECK
entries.fragment: Main scheme cards cannot be discarded from play.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: The words “max” and “maximum” impose a maximum across all copies of a card (by title) for all players.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: ”Max X per [period]” imposes a maximum number of times that copies of that card can be played during the designated time period.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: If a card with a maximum is canceled, the card is still counted toward the maximum.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: “Max X per deck” restricts the number of copies of that card that may be included in each player deck.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: “Max 1 per player” is player specific, and restricts the number of copies of that card that each player may control in play at a given time.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: A player cannot take control of another copy of a “Max 1 per player” card they already control.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: “Max 1 per [game element]” restricts the number of copies of that card that can be attached to each indicated game element.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: “Max 1 per [instance]” restricts the number of times an ability can be triggered by a single instance of a triggering effect across all copies of the card with the maximum.

entries.title: MAX, MAXIMUM
entries.fragment: The parenthetical “(to a maximum of [value])” within an ability imposes a maximum on that ability for the duration of that ability.

entries.title: MAXIMUM HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: A character’s maximum hit points is their base hit points plus or minus all “gets” hit point modifiers that are active on that character.

entries.title: MAY
entries.fragment: The word “may” indicates that a specified player has the option to resolve the text that follows.

entries.title: MENTAL RESOURCE
entries.fragment: A mental resource ([mental]) is one of the four types of resources.

entries.title: MENTAL RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Mental resources can be spent to pay the resource cost of cards and abilities.

entries.title: MENTAL RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Some card abilities specifically require mental resources to be spent in order to resolve their effects.

entries.title: MINION
entries.fragment: Minion is an encounter card type.

entries.title: MINION
entries.fragment: If a minion enters play, it remains in play until a card ability or game effect causes it to leave play.

entries.title: MINION
entries.fragment: If a minion has zero or fewer remaining hit points, it is defeated and discarded.

entries.title: MINION
entries.fragment: Minions engaged with a player activate (one minion at a time and in an order of the engaged player’s choosing) during step two of the villain phase, after the villain activates.

entries.title: MINION
entries.fragment: If a minion engages a player during an enemy activation in which all minions engaged with that player are instructed to activate (such as through a “Boost” ability during step two of the villain phase), the newly-engaged minion will also activate.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Before starting a game of Marvel Champions, players can customize their experience by choosing from or combining different modes of play.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: To play in Standard Mode, follow the content and setup instructions for the chosen scenario.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: To play a standard game modified by expert mode, follow the content and setup instructions for the chosen scenario, using the listed expert mode villain stages, and add the Expert encounter set to encounter deck.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Expert mode can also be combined with heroic mode, skirmish mode, and/or campaign mode.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: To play a standard game modified by heroic mode, before the game begins, the player group chooses a heroic level number (such as heroic level 1 or 4).

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Heroic mode can also be combined with expert mode, skirmish mode, and/or campaign mode.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: To play a standard game modified by skirmish mode, before the game begins, the player group chooses any one version of the villain.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Skirmish mode can also be combined with expert mode, heroic mode, and/or campaign mode.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Expert campaign mode is a modification of campaign mode for advanced players who seek a greater challenge.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Each campaign comes with its own campaign log.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: If a card is removed from a campaign, that card can no longer be used during the rest of the campaign, even if players retry the scenario wherein that card was removed.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: During campaign mode or expert campaign mode, players can choose which other mode(s) they wish to play for each individual scenario.

entries.title: MODES OF PLAY
entries.fragment: Campaign mode (and expert campaign mode) can also be combined with expert mode, heroic mode, and/or skirmish mode.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: The game constantly checks and (if necessary) updates the count of any variable quantity that is being modified.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: The “per player” icon ([per-player]) is not considered a modifier and is applied before any modifiers are applied.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: The calculation of a value treats all modifiers as being applied simultaneously.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: If a value is “set” to a specific number, the set modifier overrides all non-set modifiers.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: After all active modifiers have been taken into account, if a value is below zero, it is treated as zero: a card cannot have “negative” icons, attributes, traits, cost, or keywords.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: Fractional values are rounded up after all modifiers have been applied.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: If a card ability causes a character to “get” a statistic (such as +1 ATK or 4 hit points), the ability modifies the character’s statistic while it is active.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: If such an ability expires or otherwise becomes inactive, the modified statistic reverts to the value it would have without the modifier.

entries.title: MODIFIERS
entries.fragment: A value of a dash (–) cannot be modified.

entries.title: MODULAR ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: Cards belonging to a “modular encounter set” (or sometimes “modular set”) are a classification of encounter card that can be added to and/or removed from nearly any scenario.

entries.title: MODULAR ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: During game setup, many scenarios will instruct the players on how many modular encounter sets must be included in that scenario.

entries.title: MODULAR ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: If a modular encounter set is added to a scenario, it is done so as an entire set.

entries.title: MODULAR ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: A modular encounter set card is designated by the modular encounter set’s name with which it is associated printed at the bottom of the card in its encounter set name area.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: Some abilities allow players to move game elements, such as cards, damage, or threat.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: When an element moves, it cannot move to its same (current) placement.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If there is no valid source or destination for a move, the move cannot be made.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: It is possible for damage to move between dials and cards (and vice versa).

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If damage is moved from a dial to a card, increase the hit points tracked by the dial by the specified amount (no higher than the card’s maximum hit points), and place the same amount of damage on the card.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If damage is moved from a card to a dial, remove damage from the card and reduce the dial by the same amount.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If damage is moved off a character, the moved damage is considered to be healed from that character.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If damage is moved to a character, the moved damage is considered to be dealt to that character.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If threat is moved off a scheme, the moved threat is considered to be removed from that scheme.

entries.title: MOVE
entries.fragment: If threat is moved to a scheme, the moved threat is considered to be placed on that scheme.

entries.title: NEMESIS ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: Each identity in the game comes with an associated nemesis encounter set.

entries.title: NEMESIS ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: A nemesis encounter set is a subset of an identity- specific set.

entries.title: NEMESIS ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: A nemesis set cards may only be used alongside an identity if those cards share a set icon with that identity.

entries.title: NEMESIS ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: An identity’s “nemesis minion” is the minion belonging to that identity’s nemesis set.

entries.title: NEMESIS ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: If a nemesis set has multiple minions in it, the “nemesis minion” is designated by parenthetical text printed on one or more of those minions.

entries.title: NEMESIS ENCOUNTER SET
entries.fragment: An identity’s “nemesis side scheme” is the side scheme belonging to that identity’s nemesis set.

entries.title: NON-NUMERICAL VARIABLE
entries.fragment: If a non-numerical variable (such as a letter or other symbol) is defined to have a numerical value (such as a card ability assigning a value to ‘X’), treat that variable as the defined value.

entries.title: NON-NUMERICAL VARIABLE
entries.fragment: For costs involving the letter X, the value of X is defined by card ability or player choice, after which the amount paid may be modified by effects without changing the value of X.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: Obligation is an encounter card type that represents a commitment or obstacle that an identity’s alter-ego might have to face or overcome.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: Abilities on obligations that use the words “you” or “your” apply only to the player whose play area the obligation is in.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: Each identity is associated with one or more obligation cards.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: Identity-specific obligation cards are part of their associated identity’s identity-specific set.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: Identity-specific obligation cards can only be used alongside an identity if those cards share a set icon with that identity.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: If an obligation cannot be given to the specified player for any reason, ignore the card’s ability, remove it from the game, and reveal an additional encounter card.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: Only the player with the obligation in their play area can trigger abilities or pay costs on that obligation.

entries.title: OBLIGATION
entries.fragment: The player does not draw a card to replace the obligation unless they are refilling their hand to their hand size.

entries.title: “OTHERWISE”
entries.fragment: Effects beginning with “otherwise” resolve only if the preceding effect was not resolved.

entries.title: “OTHERWISE”
entries.fragment: An “otherwise” effect will resolve if one or more of the following are true of the preceding effect:

entries.title: “OTHERWISE”
entries.fragment: It has a condition that is not true.

entries.title: “OTHERWISE”
entries.fragment: It has an effect that cannot at least partially resolve.

entries.title: “OTHERWISE”
entries.fragment: If “otherwise” is preceded by a semicolon, the “preceding effect” refers to the effects before the semicolon in the same sentence.

entries.title: OVERKILL
entries.fragment: If an ally is defeated by an attack with the overkill keyword, deal any damage on that ally beyond its hit points to the identity of the player who controls the ally.

entries.title: OVERKILL
entries.fragment: The overkill keyword is equivalent to the following ability: “If this attack defeats an ally, deal the damage beyond its hit points to the identity of that ally’s controller.

entries.title: OVERKILL
entries.fragment: Damage dealt by overkill to an identity or villain is considered damage from an attack, but does not constitute an attack against that character.

entries.title: OVERKILL
entries.fragment: If a card ability counts excess damage dealt, that ability counts the same value of excess damage that is calculated when resolving the overkill keyword.

entries.title: OVERKILL
entries.fragment: If excess damage from an attack with overkill is prevented, that damage is not dealt to the identity or villain.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: A card’s owner is the player whose deck contained the card at the start of setup.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: Identity cards are owned and controlled by the player playing as that identity.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: Cards enter play under their owner’s control.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: Upgrades attached to a card controlled by a player other than the upgrade’s owner are controlled by that other player.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: When a player takes control of a campaign-specific or scenario-specific player card (such as an ally, support, or upgrade) with a player card back, that player becomes the owner of that card until the game ends or another player takes control of that card.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: Control of a card remains constant unless an ability explicitly causes the card to change control.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: A player controls the cards in their own out-of-play areas (such as the hand, the deck, and the discard pile).

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: If a character changes control while it is in play, it remains in the same state (i.e., readied or exhausted, damaged or not, etc.) and is moved to its new controller’s play area.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: Upgrades on a card that changes control also change control to the same new controller.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: A change in control of a card remains in effect until one of the following occurs:

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: The ability that changed control of that card ceases to be in effect (for instance, when an attachment or upgrade that changes control of the attached card is removed), that card reverts to its owner’s control.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: That card leaves play, it is placed in its owner’s equivalent out-of-play area (hand, deck, or discard pile, or removed from the game if that player is no longer in the game).

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: That card is an event that was played, it is placed in its owner’s discard pile.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: That card is discarded from a player’s hand, it is placed in its owner’s discard pile.

entries.title: OWNERSHIP AND CONTROL
entries.fragment: If a game step or card ability references a card that “you control” or a “player controls,” that game step or card ability only refers to cards in play currently under that player’s control.

entries.title: PATROL
entries.fragment: While a minion with the patrol keyword is engaged with a player, that player cannot use cards they control to thwart the main scheme.

entries.title: PATROL
entries.fragment: The patrol keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “The engaged player cannot thwart the main scheme.”

entries.title: PER PLAYER ICON
entries.fragment: The [per-player] icon next to a value multiplies that value by the number of players who started the scenario.

entries.title: PER PLAYER ICON
entries.fragment: If a player is eliminated, this value does not change.

entries.title: PERIL
entries.fragment: While a player is resolving a card with the peril keyword, that player cannot consult other players, and other players cannot play cards or trigger abilities.

entries.title: PERIL
entries.fragment: The peril keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “While a player is resolving this card, that player cannot consult other players, and other players cannot trigger abilities.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: A card with the permanent keyword cannot be defeated, leave play, or have any part of its text box blanked, except by card abilities in the same set (hero set, scenario set, or modular set).

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: The permanent keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “Set this card aside during setup.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: Permanent cards are set aside before step 1 of setup and are put into play later by abilities on other cards.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: Permanent cards do not count towards a player’s minimum or maximum deck size.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: Permanent cards are not valid targets for card effects that would cause the permanent card to leave play.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: If a permanent card would be targeted by such an effect (for example, “discard the lowest-cost support you control”), that effect instead targets the non-permanent card that fits its criteria.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: If the card to which a permanent attachment was attached leaves play, resolve that attachment’s “attach to” text.

entries.title: PERMANENT
entries.fragment: If a player is eliminated from the game while a non-attachment permanent card they do not own is in their play area, remove that permanent card from the game.

entries.title: PHYSICAL RESOURCE
entries.fragment: A physical resource ([physical]) is one of the four types of resources.

entries.title: PHYSICAL RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Physical resources can be spent to pay the resource cost of cards and abilities.

entries.title: PHYSICAL RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Some card abilities specifically require physical resources to be spent in order to resolve their effects.

entries.title: PIERCING
entries.fragment: An attack with the piercing keyword discards any tough status cards from the attacked character before dealing damage.

entries.title: PIERCING
entries.fragment: The piercing keyword is equivalent to the following ability: “Before this attack deals damage to a character, discard each tough status card from that character.”

entries.title: PIERCING
entries.fragment: If an attack with the piercing keyword would deal no damage to the attacked character, it does not discard tough status cards from that character.

entries.title: PLAY, PUT INTO PLAY
entries.fragment: Playing a card involves paying the card’s cost and placing the card in the play area.

entries.title: PLAY, PUT INTO PLAY
entries.fragment: Cards with the text “[type] form only” can only be played or put into play by a player whose identity is in the specified form.

entries.title: PLAY, PUT INTO PLAY
entries.fragment: When an event card is played, place it on the table, resolve its ability, and place the card in its owner’s discard pile.

entries.title: PLAY, PUT INTO PLAY
entries.fragment: A card that is put into play is not considered to have been played.

entries.title: PLAY, PUT INTO PLAY
entries.fragment: When a card is put into play, its resource cost is ignored.

entries.title: PLAY, PUT INTO PLAY
entries.fragment: Unless otherwise stated by the “put into play” effect, cards that are put into play must do so in a play area or state that matches the rules of playing the card.

entries.title: PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: There are two types of play areas: a player’s play area and the villain’s play area.

entries.title: PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: A player’s play area contains that player’s identity, deck, hand, discard pile, any cards in play under their control, and any faceup or facedown encounter cards in their play area (such as engaged minions or encounter cards that have been dealt to them).

entries.title: PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: The villain’s play area contains the villain deck, main scheme deck, encounter deck, encounter discard pile, and any encounter cards in play that have not entered a player’s play area (such as side schemes or environments).

entries.title: PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: A card cannot be in more than one play area at a time.

entries.title: PLAY RESTRICTIONS AND PERMISSIONS
entries.fragment: Many cards and abilities contain specific instructions pertaining to when or how they may or may not be used, or to specific conditions that must be true in order to use them.

entries.title: PLAY RESTRICTIONS AND PERMISSIONS
entries.fragment: In order to use an ability or play a card, all of its play restrictions must be observed.

entries.title: PLAY RESTRICTIONS AND PERMISSIONS
entries.fragment: A permission is an optional play restriction, which allows a player to play a card or use an ability outside the timing or specifications provided by the game rules.

entries.title: PLAYER
entries.fragment: A player is a person who is playing in a game of Marvel Champions.

entries.title: PLAYER
entries.fragment: Each player in the game has their own personal play area containing their identity card, their identity’s hit point dial, their hand of cards, their deck that they draw from, their discard pile that they place their discarded cards into, any allies, upgrades, or supports that they may have in play, and any attachments, minions, or obligations that they may have in their play area.

entries.title: PLAYER
entries.fragment: During each player phase of each round, each player takes their own personal turn where they can play cards, perform actions with cards they control, and use various abilities.

entries.title: PLAYER
entries.fragment: Each player owns the cards that were contained within their deck (including their identity card) at the start of the game.

entries.title: PLAYER
entries.fragment: Some game steps, game functions, or card abilities may refer to the “first player”.

entries.title: PLAYER CARD
entries.fragment: There are seven player card types: ally cards, event cards, identity cards, player side scheme cards, resource cards, support cards, and upgrade cards.

entries.title: PLAYER CARD
entries.fragment: Player cards may belong to various classifications, such as identity-specific player cards or aspect player cards.

entries.title: PLAYER CARD
entries.fragment: Most player cards have a blue card back.

entries.title: PLAYER DECK
entries.fragment: A player’s deck contains the player cards (allies, events, player side schemes, resources, supports, and upgrades) owned by the player who started the game with that deck.

entries.title: PLAYER DECK
entries.fragment: The order of cards within a player’s deck cannot be changed unless a player is instructed to do so by a game step, game function, or card ability.

entries.title: PLAYER DECK
entries.fragment: If the player’s deck empties and reshuffles while the player was drawing cards, the player continues to draw cards up to the specified number.

entries.title: PLAYER DECK
entries.fragment: If the player’s deck empties while the player was discarding cards from their deck, no further cards are discarded from the newly shuffled deck.

entries.title: PLAYER DECK
entries.fragment: If a player deck empties and the player has no cards in their discard pile, the deck does not reset until there is at least one card in the player’s discard pile, then the player deals themself one facedown encounter card.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: A player is eliminated from the game if their identity is defeated.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: If that card is an attachment with the permanent keyword, resolve its “attach to” text.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: Remove each non-attachment card with the permanent keyword from the game.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: Place each other card in its owner’s discard pile.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: If all players are eliminated, the game ends and the players lose.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: If a player is eliminated partway through the resolution of an ability, resolve the entire ability.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: If a player is eliminated in the middle of an attack, that attack ends.

entries.title: PLAYER ELIMINATION
entries.fragment: Effects that refer to the players in the game ignore eliminated players, except for the per player icon ([per-player]).

entries.title: PLAYER PHASE
entries.fragment: During the player phase, each player (in player order) takes one turn.

entries.title: PLAYER PHASE
entries.fragment: Effects that last “until the end of the [player] phase” end after players draw up to their hand size and all cards are readied.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Player side schemes are missions the heroes undertake to facilitate defeating the villain.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: When a player side scheme enters play, it is placed next to the main scheme in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Each player side scheme enters play with an amount of threat on it equal to its starting threat value.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: The number of player side schemes in play at any time is limited by the player side scheme limit.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: A player side scheme remains in play until either there is no threat on it (which causes it to be defeated and either discarded or, if it has the victory X keyword, added to the victory display) or it is discarded due to there being more player side schemes in play than the limit.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Any rules or card effects that refer to “schemes” or “side schemes” also refer to player side schemes.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Heroes and allies can remove threat from a player side scheme by performing a basic thwart.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Abilities that remove threat from “a scheme” or “a side scheme” can remove threat from a player side scheme.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME LIMIT
entries.fragment: The number of player side schemes in play at any time is limited by the player side scheme limit.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME LIMIT
entries.fragment: If one or two players started the game, the player side scheme limit is one.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME LIMIT
entries.fragment: If there are ever more player side schemes in play than the limit, the first player chooses and discards player side schemes until there are no longer more in play than the limit.

entries.title: PLAYER SIDE SCHEME LIMIT
entries.fragment: A player may play a player side scheme even while at the player side scheme limit.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: During their turn, a player may perform the following options, in any order.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: Change form from hero to alter-ego, or from alter- ego to hero.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: Play an ally, upgrade, support, or player side scheme card from hand.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: Use their alter-ego’s basic recovery (if in alter-ego form) or their hero’s basic attack or thwart power (if in hero form).

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: Use an ally card they control in play to attack an enemy or thwart a scheme.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: Trigger an “Action” ability on: a.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: If the action ability is preceded by “Hero” or “Alter- Ego”, the player must be in the specified form in order to trigger the ability.

entries.title: PLAYER TURN
entries.fragment: Ask another player to trigger any “Action” ability that player could trigger on their own turn.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: A player’s play area (also sometimes referred to as a “player’s game area”) is the area of play where a player’s identity card, deck, hand, discard pile, and hit point dial are located.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Ally cards, support cards, and upgrade cards are placed in a player’s play area when they enter play.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Attachment cards attached to cards in the villain’s play area are not in the player’s play area.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Minion cards engaged with a player are in that player’s play area and not in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Obligation cards given to a player are in that player’s play area and not in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: While card abilities can affect cards across play areas, unless a game rule or card ability states otherwise, cards cannot be played into another player’s play area.

entries.title: PLAYER’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: If a player is eliminated from the game (through their identity being defeated, or otherwise), their play area is removed from the game.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: Some card abilities prevent damage or threat.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: When damage is prevented, reduce the amount of damage the target takes (i.e.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: When an effect prevents damage dealt to a character, the amount of damage that character “takes” is reduced, but the amount of damage “dealt” is not reduced.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: If an effect prevents all damage dealt to a character, that character is not considered to have taken damage.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: If all damage from an attack is prevented, the attacking character is considered to have dealt damage, but is not considered to have “attacked and damaged” the attacked character.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: If dealing damage is a cost, that cost is considered paid even if some or all of that damage is prevented.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: If taking damage is a cost, that cost is not considered paid unless all of that damage was taken.

entries.title: PREVENT
entries.fragment: When threat is prevented, reduce the amount of threat being assigned before it is placed on the scheme.

entries.title: PRINTED
entries.fragment: The word “printed” refers to the text, characteristic, or value that is physically printed on the card.

entries.title: PRINTED
entries.fragment: If a player must pay a cost using “printed resources,” they may use resources generated by a card’s ability, so long as the icon(s) for the resource(s) that card generates is printed in its text box.

entries.title: PRINTED
entries.fragment: Wild resources ([wild]) cannot be spent as other resource types for such a cost.

entries.title: QUALIFIERS
entries.fragment: If ability text includes a qualifier followed by multiple terms, the qualifier applies to each item in the list, if applicable.

entries.title: QUICKSTRIKE
entries.fragment: After a minion with the quickstrike keyword engages a player whose identity is in hero form, that minion attacks that player.

entries.title: QUICKSTRIKE
entries.fragment: The quickstrike keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Response (Hero): After this minion engages a player, it attacks that player.”

entries.title: QUICKSTRIKE
entries.fragment: If a minion with the quickstrike keyword is being revealed, the quickstrike keyword resolves after any “When Revealed” abilities on that minion are resolved.

entries.title: RANGED
entries.fragment: An attack with the ranged keyword ignores the retaliate keyword.

entries.title: RANGED
entries.fragment: The ranged keyword is equivalent to the following ability: “This attack ignores the retaliate keyword.”

entries.title: READY
entries.fragment: Cards enter play in a ready state, positioned so that their controller can read their text from left to right.

entries.title: READY
entries.fragment: If a player is instructed to ready an exhausted card, the card is returned to its ready state.

entries.title: READY
entries.fragment: If there is an additional cost for a player to ready a card, that player can choose not to pay that cost.

entries.title: RECOVER, RECOVERY
entries.fragment: Recovery is a basic power a player can use in alter-ego form.

entries.title: RECOVER, RECOVERY
entries.fragment: An identity that has no damage to heal cannot perform a basic recovery.

entries.title: REFERENTIAL ABILITY
entries.fragment: Some abilities refer to specific cards by name.

entries.title: REMAINING HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: A character’s remaining hit points is the amount of damage that character can take before reaching zero hit points.

entries.title: REMAINING HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: An identity’s or villain’s hit point dial represents their remaining hit points.

entries.title: REMAINING HIT POINTS
entries.fragment: To calculate remaining hit points for an ally or minion, start with the character’s maximum hit points (as indicated by its printed value modified by any card abilities or game effects), and subtract their sustained damage (the number of damage counters on them).

entries.title: REMINDER TEXT
entries.fragment: Some card abilities may include reminder text.

entries.title: REMOVED FROM THE GAME
entries.fragment: A card that has been removed from the game is set aside and does not interact with the game in any manner for the duration of its removal.

entries.title: REMOVED FROM THE GAME
entries.fragment: “Removed from the game” is an out-of-play state.

entries.title: REMOVED FROM THE GAME
entries.fragment: A card that has been removed from the game cannot reenter the game through any means.

entries.title: REPLACEMENT EFFECT
entries.fragment: A replacement effect replaces a specified effect with a different effect.

entries.title: REPLACEMENT EFFECT
entries.fragment: When an effect is replaced, it is no longer considered imminent and no further interrupts or responses to that effect can be triggered.

entries.title: REQUIREMENT (RESOURCES)
entries.fragment: A card with the requirement keyword cannot be played unless each resource of the specified type is spent while paying for that card’s cost.

entries.title: REQUIREMENT (RESOURCES)
entries.fragment: The requirement (resources) keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “When paying this card’s resource cost, you must spend the following resources: [resources].”

entries.title: REQUIREMENT (RESOURCES)
entries.fragment: A card with the requirement keyword cannot be played “ignoring its resource cost” because the required resources cannot be paid for it.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: Effects, abilities, event cards, and treachery cards are each resolved under the following conditions:

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: An effect is resolved when it is applied to the game state.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: An ability is resolved when it is triggered and one or more of its effects resolve.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: An event card is resolved when it is played and one or more of its abilities resolve.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: A treachery card is resolved when it is revealed and one or more of its abilities resolve.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: Constant abilities are never considered resolved.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: Card types other than events and treacheries are not considered resolved, though abilities on those other card types can be resolved.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: If all of the effects of an ability are canceled, that ability is not considered to have resolved.

entries.title: RESOLVE
entries.fragment: If all of the abilities of an event or treachery are canceled, that card is not considered to have resolved.

entries.title: RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Resources are used to pay the cost to play cards and to pay certain ability costs.

entries.title: RESOURCE
entries.fragment: A player can generate resources to pay a cost by discarding cards from their hand to generate the resource or resources indicated at the bottom-left corner of the card, or by using card abilities that generate resources.

entries.title: RESOURCE
entries.fragment: There are four types of resources in the game: energy ([energy]), mental ([mental]), and physical ([physical]), and wild ([wild]).

entries.title: RESOURCE
entries.fragment: To pay the cost of playing a card, a number of resources equal to (or greater than) the card’s cost must be generated.

entries.title: RESOURCE
entries.fragment: If an ability has a resource cost, a number of resources equal to or greater than this cost must be generated.

entries.title: RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Excess resources generated toward any cost are lost, and do not carry over to future costs.

entries.title: RESOURCE ABILITY
entries.fragment: A resource ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “Resource” timing trigger.

entries.title: RESOURCE ABILITY
entries.fragment: A resource ability can be triggered anytime the player who controls the ability is generating resources to pay a cost.

entries.title: RESOURCE ABILITY
entries.fragment: A resource ability that generates a resource only for a specific type of cost cannot be triggered when paying a cost not of that type.

entries.title: RESOURCE CARD
entries.fragment: Resource cards are a player card type.

entries.title: RESOURCE CARD
entries.fragment: Some resource cards have card text that is active while using the card to generate resources.

entries.title: RESOURCE CARD
entries.fragment: Resource cards are considered to be an extension of an identity.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: A response ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “Response” timing trigger.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: Players can only trigger response abilities on cards they control or on encounter cards.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: Players cannot trigger response abilities on obligations in other players’ play areas.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: Multiple responses may be triggered from the same triggering condition, but each response may only be triggered once per occurrence of the triggering condition.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: Multiple copies of a card with a response can each be triggered by the same triggering condition.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: If single effect causes multiple triggering conditions to occur, responses to each of those triggering conditions can be resolved in any order.

entries.title: RESPONSE
entries.fragment: Once all players decide they do not wish to resolve any (further) responses to a triggering condition, (further) responses to that instance of that triggering condition cannot be used.

entries.title: RESTRICTED
entries.fragment: A player cannot have more than two cards with the restricted keyword in play under their control at the same time.

entries.title: RESTRICTED
entries.fragment: The restricted keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Response: After you take control of this card, if you control more than 2 restricted cards, discard all but 2 of those cards.”

entries.title: RETALIATE X
entries.fragment: After a character with the retaliate X keyword is attacked, deal X damage to the attacker.

entries.title: RETALIATE X
entries.fragment: The retaliate X keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Response: After this character is attacked, deal X damage to the attacker.”

entries.title: RETALIATE X
entries.fragment: The character with retaliate X must be in play after the attack resolves to deal this damage.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: During step four of the villain phase, each player (in player order) reveals and resolves all facedown encounter cards that have been dealt to them, one card at a time in the order in which they were dealt.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Attachment: It enters play attached to the game element specified by its “attach to” text.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Environment: It enters play in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Minion: It enters play in the play area of the player revealing it.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Obligation: It enters play in the play area of the player revealing it.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: If the card specifies a player to give it to, that player is considered to be revealing it.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Side scheme: It enters play in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Treachery: Place it on the table in front of the player revealing it.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Other: Place it on the table in front of the player revealing it.

entries.title: REVEAL
entries.fragment: Responses (both forced and non-forced) to any step of the revealing of an encounter card are not resolved until after all steps of the reveal process have been completed.
