entries.title: SCENARIO-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: Cards in the “scenario-specific” classification are cards that belong to a scenario’s set of accompanying cards.

entries.title: SCENARIO-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: A scenario must include each scenario-specific card associated with that scenario.

entries.title: SCENARIO-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: In most scenarios, the scenario-specific cards are separated into three decks: the villain deck (comprised of that scenario’s villain cards), the main scheme deck (comprised of that scenario’s main scheme cards), and the encounter deck (comprised of that scenario’s attachment, environment, minion, side scheme, and treachery cards).

entries.title: SCENARIO-SPECIFIC CARD
entries.fragment: A scenario-specific card is designated by the name of the scenario with which it is associated printed at the bottom of the card in its encounter set name area.

entries.title: SCHEME (CARD TYPE)
entries.fragment: The word “scheme” denotes three different card types: main schemes, player side schemes, and side schemes.

entries.title: SCHEME (CARD TYPE)
entries.fragment: If a card ability places threat on or removes threat from “a scheme,” the player resolving that ability chooses which scheme—main scheme or side schemes—that ability affects.

entries.title: SCHEME (ENEMY ACTIVATION)
entries.fragment: A scheme is a type of enemy activation.

entries.title: SEARCH
entries.fragment: When a player is instructed to search for a card, the player is permitted to look at each of the cards in the searched area.

entries.title: SEARCH
entries.fragment: If a player finds multiple cards that satisfy the criteria of a search, the player chooses among those options.

entries.title: SEARCH
entries.fragment: Cards being searched are not considered to leave the searched area.

entries.title: SEARCH
entries.fragment: If any portion of a deck is searched, upon completion of that game step, game function, or card ability, shuffle that entire deck.

entries.title: SEARCH
entries.fragment: If a player is instructed to “search [their] collection” for a card, the player looks through all of their Marvel Champions cards outside of the current game for the specified card.

entries.title: SEARCH
entries.fragment: They become the owner of that card until the end of the game.

entries.title: SET ASIDE, SET-ASIDE
entries.fragment: Some game steps or card abilities instruct players to set aside specific cards.

entries.title: SET ICON
entries.fragment: The set icon is an indicator on a card of that card’s product of origin, located in the card’s collector information at the bottom of the card.

entries.title: SETUP (KEYWORD)
entries.fragment: A card with the setup keyword begins the game in play.

entries.title: SETUP (KEYWORD)
entries.fragment: Cards with the setup keyword are put into play during the “Put Setup Cards Into Play” step of setup.

entries.title: SETUP (TRIGGERED ABILITY)
entries.fragment: “Setup” is a type of triggered ability that is resolved during setup.

entries.title: SETUP (TRIGGERED ABILITY)
entries.fragment: Setup abilities are mandatory.

entries.title: SETUP (TRIGGERED ABILITY)
entries.fragment: Setup abilities on encounter cards are resolved during the “Resolve Scenario Setup and When Revealed Abilities” step of setup.

entries.title: SETUP (TRIGGERED ABILITY)
entries.fragment: Setup abilities on player cards are resolved during the “Resolve Character Setup Abilities” step of setup.

entries.title: SHUFFLE
entries.fragment: Shuffling is the game function of randomizing the contents of a deck.

entries.title: SHUFFLE
entries.fragment: If a player is instructed to shuffle a deck, that deck must be randomized to the point where no player within the game can ascertain the order of the cards within that deck.

entries.title: SHUFFLE
entries.fragment: Any time a deck is searched by a game step or card ability, that deck is shuffled after the game step or card ability completes its resolution.

entries.title: SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Side scheme is an encounter card type that represents additional obstacles and distractions the heroes are confronted with.

entries.title: SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: Each side scheme enters play with an amount of threat on it equal to the card’s starting threat value (indicated at the bottom of the card).

entries.title: SIDE SCHEME
entries.fragment: A side scheme remains in play until there is no threat on it (which causes it to be defeated and discarded), or until a card ability removes it from play.

entries.title: SIMULTANEOUS RESOLUTION
entries.fragment: If two or more effects with the same bold timing trigger would resolve simultaneously, the first player determines the order in which the effects resolve.

entries.title: SPECIAL
entries.fragment: A special ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “Special” timing trigger.

entries.title: STALWART
entries.fragment: A character that has the stalwart keyword cannot be stunned or confused.

entries.title: STALWART
entries.fragment: The stalwart keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “This character cannot have confused or stunned status cards.”

entries.title: STALWART
entries.fragment: If a character gains the stalwart keyword while they have a stunned and/or confused status card, each stunned and/or confused status card is removed from that character.

entries.title: STANDARD SET
entries.fragment: The standard set is an encounter set that is added to most scenarios.

entries.title: STANDARD SET
entries.fragment: The standard set is not a modular encounter set and cannot be selected (by the players or randomly) when a scenario requires players to choose a modular encounter set to include in that scenario.

entries.title: STANDARD SET
entries.fragment: Cards in the “Standard” classification are any cards that have the word “Standard” printed by the bottom of the card in its encounter set name area.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: A star icon is used in conjunction with a card’s stat or boost field to indicate that there is a mandatory ability in the text box that corresponds to that field.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: If a star icon is located next to an enemy’s ATK or SCH value, the icon serves as a reminder to check that enemy’s text box whenever that enemy uses that value to attack or scheme.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: If a star icon is located in the ATK or SCH field of an attachment, the icon serves as a reminder to check that attachment’s text box whenever the attached enemy uses the value that field is modifying to attack or scheme.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: If a star icon is located next to an ally’s ATK or THW value, the icon serves as a reminder to check that ally’s text box whenever that ally uses that value to attack or thwart.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: If a star icon is located next to a hero’s ATK, THW, or DEF, or next to an alter-ego’s REC value, the icon serves as a reminder to check that character’s text box whenever they use that value to attack, thwart, defend, or recover.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: If a game step or ability references a power with the value of star ([star]), that value is defined in that card’s text.

entries.title: STAR ICON
entries.fragment: If a star icon is located in an encounter card’s boost field, the icon serves as a reminder to check that card’s text box whenever that card is turned face up as a boost card during the villain’s activation.

entries.title: STATUS CARDS
entries.fragment: Status card represent different states a character may find themselves in during the game.

entries.title: STATUS CARDS
entries.fragment: A character cannot have more than one status card of each type at a time.

entries.title: STATUS CARDS
entries.fragment: Characters with the steady keyword can have one additional confused status card and one additional stunned status card.

entries.title: STATUS CARDS
entries.fragment: Status card abilities have timing priority over all conflicting triggered abilities.

entries.title: STEADY
entries.fragment: A character with the steady keyword can have one additional stunned status card and one additional confused status card.

entries.title: STEADY
entries.fragment: The steady keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “This character can have 1 additional confused status card and 1 additional stunned status card.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: Stun is a status that cancels a character’s next attack.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: A stunned status card resolves like the triggered ability: “Forced Interrupt: When this character would attack, remove each stunned status card from it instead.”

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: If an ability “stuns” a character, give that character a stunned status card.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: A character is stunned if it has a stunned status card.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: A character with the steady keyword is stunned only if it has two stunned status cards.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: If a character has an ability stating that it “cannot be stunned,” stunned status cards cannot be placed on that character.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: If a stunned identity or ally attempts to attack or use an attack ability, discard the stunned card instead.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: A stunned character can attempt to attack or use an attack ability even if it has no valid target for an attack.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: If a stunned villain or minion would attack, discard the stunned status card instead.

entries.title: STUN, STUNNED
entries.fragment: As the attack action or attack activation was replaced by the removal of the stunned status card, that character is not considered to have attacked.

entries.title: SUBTITLE
entries.fragment: Some ally cards have a subtitle beneath the title.

entries.title: SUPPORT
entries.fragment: Support is a player card type that represent locations, backline supporters or friends, and other behind-the-scenes elements a hero or alter-ego might have at their disposal.

entries.title: SUPPORT
entries.fragment: Support cards enter play in the back row of a player’s play area.

entries.title: SUPPORT
entries.fragment: A support card is active while it is in play, and it remains in play until a card ability causes it to leave play.

entries.title: SUPPORT
entries.fragment: Attacks, thwarts, defenses, action abilities, and triggered abilities that resolve from supports in play under a player’s control are not considered to be performed by that player’s identity.

entries.title: SURGE
entries.fragment: When an encounter card with this keyword is revealed, the player resolving the card deals themself a facedown encounter card from the top of the encounter deck.

entries.title: SURGE
entries.fragment: The surge keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “When Revealed: Deal yourself 1 facedown encounter card.”

entries.title: SURGE
entries.fragment: Complete the process of resolving the original card, as well as any response abilities that are triggered by that card being revealed, before revealing the additional card.

entries.title: SUSTAINED DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Sustained damage refers to the difference between a character’s maximum hit points and remaining hit points.

entries.title: SUSTAINED DAMAGE
entries.fragment: To calculate sustained damage for an identity or villain (using a hit point dial), start with the character’s maximum hit points (as indicated by its printed value modified by any card abilities or game effects), and subtract their remaining hit points (as indicated by the dial).

entries.title: SUSTAINED DAMAGE
entries.fragment: Sustained damage on an ally or minion is equal to the total value of all damage tokens on the card.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: An instruction to “swap” two components means to exchange the location of those two components.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: A swap cannot be completed if there is not a component in both locations.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: For example, you cannot “swap a card in your hand with the top card of your deck” if you have no cards in hand.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: Swapped cards maintain the orientation (such as ready or exhausted, faceup or facedown) of the original card.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: Swapping a card in hand with the top card of a deck is not considered drawing that card.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: When swapping a card in a play area with a card in an out-of-play area, if those two cards:

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: Share a title, neither card is considered to enter or leave play.

entries.title: “SWAP”
entries.fragment: Do not share a title, the in-play card is considered to leave play and the out-of-play card is considered to enter play.

entries.title: TABLE TALK
entries.fragment: Players are permitted and encouraged to talk to one another during play, and to work as a team to plan and execute the best course of action.

entries.title: TABLE TALK
entries.fragment: While resolving an encounter card with the peril keyword, players are not permitted to consult with one another.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: If a game function or card ability is directed toward a game element (such as an attack that deals damage to an enemy), that game element becomes the target of that function or ability for the duration of that function’s or ability’s resolution.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: Examples of targets include but are not limited to: “the villain,” “a minion,” “an enemy,” “a scheme,” “a hero,” “an ally,” “a character,” “a player,” “you,” “a card.”

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: If an ability or game function requires one or more targets, that ability or game function can only be initiated if it has at least one valid target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: Basic powers are game functions that require a valid target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: The phrase “choose a [game element]” indicates that one or more targets must be selected in order for an ability to initiate.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: Abilities that cause a player to draw one or more cards always have a valid target so long as that player has at least one card in their deck.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: A target is valid for an ability or game function if any part of that ability can affect that target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: Examples of effects on a target include but are not limited to: dealing/healing damage, adding/ removing threat, giving/removing a status card, exhausting/readying the target, defeating/ discarding the target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: Exception: A character with an ATK, SCH, or THW of 0 can perform an activation or basic power using that value against a target that is otherwise valid for that activation or basic power.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: The cost of an ability or game function is not considered when determining if that ability or game function can affect a target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: If an ability or game function has multiple effects on its target, the target is valid if at least one of those effects can affect the target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: A target is not valid for an ability if that ability would cause the target to perform a game function that another ability says the target cannot perform.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: Damage that is dealt but not taken (for example, if the damage is prevented) is considered to affect a target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: A target that “cannot take damage” is not a valid target for an ability or game function whose only effect on that target is to deal it damage.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: A target that cannot be attacked is not a valid target for an attack-labeled ability.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: A target that cannot be thwarted is not a valid target for a thwart-labeled ability.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: An ability or game function that targets multiple game elements of a specific type (for example, “each enemy”) can be initiated as along as at least one of those game elements is a valid target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: That ability or game function does not resolve against any of those game elements that is not a valid target.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: For example, the crisis ([crisis]) icon prevents threat from being removed from the main scheme.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: An ability that refers to a future target (i.e.

entries.title: TARGET
entries.fragment: An ability with a search effect requires only a searchable game area in order to initiate.

entries.title: TARGET THREAT
entries.fragment: Target threat is the amount of threat required for the main scheme deck to advance.

entries.title: TEAM-UP
entries.fragment: The team-up keyword names two characters.

entries.title: TEAM-UP
entries.fragment: The team-up (name 1 and name 2) keyword is equivalent to the following constant ability: “You cannot include this card in your deck unless your alter-ego or hero title matches name 1 or name 2.

entries.title: TEAM-UP
entries.fragment: An ally counts as a named character if either its title or subtitle matches the named character.

entries.title: TEAMWORK ()
entries.fragment: After a minion with teamwork enters play and engages a player, if there is at least one other minion that shares the specified trait in play, the minion that just entered play activates against the player it is engaged with.

entries.title: TEAMWORK ()
entries.fragment: The teamwork () keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Response: After this minion enters play, if there is another minion in play, this minion activates against the engaged player.”

entries.title: TEAMWORK ()
entries.fragment: If a minion with the teamwork keyword is being revealed, the teamwork keyword resolves after any “When Revealed” abilities on that minion are resolved.

entries.title: TEMPORARY
entries.fragment: A card with temporary must be discarded from play at the end of the round.

entries.title: TEMPORARY
entries.fragment: The temporary keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Interrupt: When the round ends, discard this card from play.”

entries.title: TEXT BOX
entries.fragment: The text box of a card is the area of a card that contains the card’s printed abilities, traits, and flavor text (if any).

entries.title: TEXT BOX
entries.fragment: If a card ability references a card’s “text box,” that ability only references the printed abilities within that card’s text box.

entries.title: TEXT BOX
entries.fragment: Icons printed within a card’s text box are considered abilities within that text box.

entries.title: “THEN”
entries.fragment: If the effect text of an ability includes the word “then”, the text preceding the word “then” must be fully true or resolved before the remainder of the effect described after the word “then” can be resolved.

entries.title: “THEN”
entries.fragment: If the pre-”then” text of an effect fully resolves, the post-”then” text of the effect must also attempt to resolve.

entries.title: “THEN”
entries.fragment: If the pre-”then” text of an effect does not fully resolve, the post-”then” text does not attempt to resolve.

entries.title: THREAT
entries.fragment: Threat tokens are used to track the amount of threat on scheme cards.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: Some game effects and card abilities reference a thwart attempt.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: A hero or ally can use their basic thwart power to thwart a scheme.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: A character can only initiate a basic thwart if there is a scheme with at least one threat for the character to remove or if that character is confused.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: An ability that allows a hero or ally to “make a basic thwart without exhausting” can allow an exhausted character to make a thwart attempt.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: If a triggered ability is labeled as a thwart—such as “Hero Action (thwart)”—resolving that ability is considered to thwart the specified scheme.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: An ability labeled as a thwart is considered a single thwart, even if that thwart removes multiple instances of threat.

entries.title: THWART
entries.fragment: If an ability increases the amount of threat an ability labeled as a thwart removes and that ability removes multiple instances of threat, each of those instances that does not use the word “additional” is increased by the specified amount.

entries.title: TOUGH
entries.fragment: Tough is a status that prevents a character from taking damage.

entries.title: TOUGH
entries.fragment: A tough status card resolves like the triggered ability: “Forced Interrupt: When this character would take damage, remove a tough status card from it instead.”

entries.title: TOUGH
entries.fragment: If a character with a tough status card would take any amount of damage, prevent all of that damage and discard a tough status card from that character instead.

entries.title: TOUGH
entries.fragment: A character with multiple tough status cards discards only one tough status card each time it would take damage.

entries.title: TOUGH
entries.fragment: When a hero with a tough status card defends an attack, they reduce the damage from the attack by their DEF first.

entries.title: TOUGH
entries.fragment: As a tough status card prevents damage fully, the character who had the tough status card is not considered to have taken damage.

entries.title: TOUGHNESS
entries.fragment: When a character with the toughness keyword enters play, place a tough status card on it.

entries.title: TOUGHNESS
entries.fragment: The toughness keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Response: After this character enters play, give it a tough status card.”

entries.title: TRAITS
entries.fragment: Many cards have one or more traits listed at the top of the text box and printed in bold italics.

entries.title: TRAITS
entries.fragment: Traits have no inherent effects on the game.

entries.title: TRAITS
entries.fragment: Traits are not considered to be part of a card’s printed text box for the purpose of card abilities.

entries.title: TREACHERY
entries.fragment: Treachery is an encounter card type that represent tactics, tricks, disasters, and other immediate occurrences that confront players during a scenario.

entries.title: TREACHERY
entries.fragment: If a treachery card is revealed from the encounter deck, the player revealing the card must resolve its effects.

entries.title: TREACHERY
entries.fragment: After resolving the effects of a treachery card (or the effects are canceled), place the card in the encounter discard pile.

entries.title: TREACHERY
entries.fragment: If a treachery causes one or more enemies to activate as its last effect, that treachery card is considered resolved and is discarded after all of those activations have resolved.

entries.title: TRIGGERED ABILITY
entries.fragment: A triggered ability is indicated by a bold timing trigger followed by a colon and the rest of the ability text.

entries.title: TRIGGERING CONDITION
entries.fragment: A triggering condition is a specific occurrence that takes place in the game.

entries.title: TRIGGERING CONDITION
entries.fragment: Each “Interrupt“ and “Response” ability can only be triggered once per occurrence of its triggering condition.

entries.title: TRIGGERING CONDITION
entries.fragment: Multiple copies of a card with an interrupt or response can each be triggered by the same triggering condition.

entries.title: TRIGGERING CONDITION
entries.fragment: If a single game occurrence creates multiple triggering conditions (such as a single attack causing a character to both take damage and be defeated), those triggering conditions are handled with a single interrupt window and a single response window.

entries.title: TUCK
entries.fragment: When a player is instructed to tuck a card under another card, they place the tucked card faceup under the other card.

entries.title: TUCK
entries.fragment: Tucked cards are not in play and are not considered “attached” to the card under which they are tucked.

entries.title: TUCK
entries.fragment: When a card leaves play, each card tucked under it is discarded.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: The unique icon indicates a card that represents a singular person, place, or thing within the Marvel universe.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: Two unique cards are considered to “match” if any of the following apply:

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: The two cards share a title, and both have no subtitle and no alter-ego title.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: The subtitle or alter-ego title of one matches the title, subtitle, or alter-ego title of the other.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: During deckbuilding, a player cannot include multiple matching cards in their deck.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: Once setup for a game has begun, a player is not prevented from adding matching cards to their deck through game effects.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: When choosing identities during setup, players cannot choose identities that match.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: The players may choose a scenario even if one or more villains match one or more chosen identities.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: A non-villain card in an out-of-play state that matches a card in play cannot enter play.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: A player card, it cannot be played or put into play.

entries.title: UNIQUE ICON
entries.fragment: A non-villain encounter card, it is discarded and any effects of it entering play are ignored.

entries.title: UPGRADE
entries.fragment: Upgrade is a player card type that represents powers, attacks, equipment, and other assets that are (in most cases) at an identity’s immediate disposal.

entries.title: UPGRADE
entries.fragment: An upgrade is active so long as it is in play, and it remains in play until a card ability causes it to leave play.

entries.title: UPGRADE
entries.fragment: Most upgrade cards enter play near a player’s identity card, and modify the player’s hero or alter-ego (or both).

entries.title: UPGRADE
entries.fragment: Some upgrades enter play and “attach to” another card.

entries.title: UPGRADE
entries.fragment: A player controls any upgrades attached to characters they control, including upgrades owned by another player.

entries.title: UPGRADE
entries.fragment: Unless attached to a different friendly character, upgrade cards are considered to be an extension of the controlling player’s identity.

entries.title: USES (X “TYPE”)
entries.fragment: When a card with this keyword enters play, place X all- purpose counters from the token pool on the card.

entries.title: USES (X “TYPE”)

entries.title: VICTORY DISPLAY
entries.fragment: The victory display is an out-of-play game area shared by all players.

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: When a card with the victory X keyword leaves play under the following conditions, place it in the victory display instead of its owner’s discard pile:

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: The victory X keyword is equivalent to the following ability based on the card with the keyword:

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: Character or side scheme: “When Defeated: Add this card to the victory display.”

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: Attachment: “Forced Interrupt: When the attached card is defeated, add this card to the victory display.”

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: Card with the uses (X “type”) keyword: “If there are no all-purpose counters on this card, add this card to the victory display instead of discarding it.”

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: A character or side scheme with the victory X keyword is placed in the victory display when it is defeated.

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: An attachment or upgrade with the victory X keyword is placed in the victory display when the card to which it is attached is defeated.

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: A card with both the victory X and uses (X “type”) keywords is placed in the victory display when its last all-purpose counter is removed from it.

entries.title: VICTORY X
entries.fragment: Some scenarios or campaigns may count the number of victory points in the victory display.

entries.title: VILLAIN, VILLAIN DECK
entries.fragment: Villain is an encounter card type that represents the primary enemy the players are attempting to defeat in a scenario.

entries.title: VILLAIN, VILLAIN DECK
entries.fragment: Villain cards cannot be discarded from play.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If the villain’s hit point dial is reduced to zero, the players have defeated that stage of the villain.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: The revealing of a villain cannot be canceled.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: Excess damage that is dealt to defeat a villain stage does not carry over to the new stage.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If the new stage of the villain has the same title as the previous stage:

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: The new stage of the villain is considered the same character as the defeated stage for purposes of card abilities (such as the retaliate X keyword).

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: Attachments, upgrades, status cards, counters, and non-damage tokens on a villain carry over to the new stage.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If the villain was defeated while activating, the villain resumes that activation using the new villain stage.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If the new stage of the villain has a different title from the previous stage:

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: The new stage of the villain not is considered the same character as the defeated stage for purposes of card abilities.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: Attachments, upgrades, status cards, counters, and non-damage tokens do not carry over to the new stage.

entries.title: VILLAIN DEFEAT
entries.fragment: If the villain was defeated while activating, the activation ends without resolving.

entries.title: VILLAIN’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: The villain’s play area (also sometimes referred to as the “villain’s game area”) is the area of play where the villain deck, the main scheme deck, the encounter deck, the encounter discard pile, and the villain’s hit point dial are located.

entries.title: VILLAIN’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Environment cards and side scheme cards are placed in the villain’s play area when they enter play.

entries.title: VILLAIN’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Attachment cards attached to cards in the villain’s play area are in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: VILLAIN’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Minion cards engaged with a player are in that player’s play area and not in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: VILLAIN’S PLAY AREA
entries.fragment: Obligation cards given to a player are in that player’s play area and not in the villain’s play area.

entries.title: VILLAINOUS
entries.fragment: When a character with the villainous keyword uses a basic power, give it a facedown boost card from the top of the encounter deck.

entries.title: VILLAINOUS
entries.fragment: The villainous keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Interrupt: When this character uses a basic power, give it a boost card.”

entries.title: VILLAINOUS
entries.fragment: If a boost ability on a boost card dealt to a character refers to “the villain,” that ability still applies to the villain (even if another type of character is resolving it).

entries.title: VULNERABLE
entries.fragment: When a character with vulnerable becomes confused or stunned, that character is immediately discarded (without being defeated).

entries.title: VULNERABLE
entries.fragment: The vulnerable keyword is equivalent to the following triggered ability: “Forced Interrupt: When this character becomes confused or stunned, discard it.”

entries.title: VULNERABLE
entries.fragment: If a character with the vulnerable keyword would simultaneously take enough damage to defeat it and become either confused or stunned, it is discarded before the damage is applied and is not considered defeated.

entries.title: VULNERABLE
entries.fragment: If a character has both the steady and vulnerable keywords, the vulnerable keyword does not take effect until that character has two confused or two stunned status cards.

entries.title: WHEN COMPLETED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: A when completed ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “When Completed” timing trigger.

entries.title: WHEN COMPLETED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: The “When Completed” timing trigger is equivalent to the following trigger: “Forced Interrupt: When this scheme is completed...”

entries.title: WHEN DEFEATED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: A when defeated ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “When Defeated” timing trigger.

entries.title: WHEN DEFEATED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: The “When Defeated” timing trigger is equivalent to the following trigger: “Forced Interrupt: When this card is defeated...”

entries.title: WHEN DEFEATED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: When a villain stage, side scheme, main scheme stage, ally, or minion is defeated, all “When Defeated” abilities on the card resolve.

entries.title: WHEN DEFEATED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: A defeated card leaves play after its “When Defeated” ability is resolved, if any.

entries.title: WHEN REVEALED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: A when revealed ability is a type of triggered ability, indicated by the bold “When Revealed” timing trigger.

entries.title: WHEN REVEALED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: If an encounter card with a “When Revealed” ability enters play during setup, resolve that ability during the “Resolve Scenario Setup and When Revealed Abilities” step.

entries.title: WHEN REVEALED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: If an encounter card with a “When Revealed” ability is put into play without being revealed, the “When Revealed” ability does not trigger.

entries.title: WHEN REVEALED ABILITIES
entries.fragment: “When Revealed” abilities on villain and main scheme cards cannot be canceled.

entries.title: WILD RESOURCE
entries.fragment: A wild resource ([wild]) is one of the four types of resources.

entries.title: WILD RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Wild resources can be spent to pay the resource cost of cards and abilities.

entries.title: WILD RESOURCE
entries.fragment: When a card that generates a wild resource has its resources doubled, each of its wild resources can be declared a different type.

entries.title: WILD RESOURCE
entries.fragment: Some card abilities specifically require wild resources to be spent in order to resolve their effects.

entries.title: WILD RESOURCE
entries.fragment: When resources are not being generated for a cost, a wild resource does not have any characteristic other than “wild resource.” In such contexts, wild resources cannot be interpreted as any of the other resource types.

entries.title: WINNING THE GAME
entries.fragment: If the final villain stage is defeated, the players win the game.

entries.title: WINNING THE GAME
entries.fragment: Some scenarios have alternate win or loss conditions.

entries.title: WINNING THE GAME
entries.fragment: Alternate win or loss conditions cannot be blanked or canceled.

entries.title: “WOULD”
entries.fragment: The word “would” is used to define the triggering condition of some interrupt abilities, and establishes a higher timing priority for those abilities than interrupts to the same triggering condition without the word “would.”

entries.title: “WOULD”
entries.fragment: If an interrupt to a triggering condition that would occur changes the nature of that which is about to occur (such as through a replacement effect), no further interrupts to the original trigger may be used since the resolution of that trigger is no longer valid.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: While resolving card abilities, if the word “you” can be resolved as referring to the player’s identity, it must be resolved as such.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a sentence uses “you” and/or “your” multiple times, all instances in that sentence refer to the same identity or player.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card deals damage to “you,” or “you” take damage, the player resolving that damage applies it to the hit point dial of their identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card ability deals indirect damage to “you,” or “you” take indirect damage, the player resolving that damage can assign that damage to characters in play under their control.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card ability exhausts “you,” the player resolving that card ability exhausts their identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card ability places a status card on “you” (such as “you are stunned”), the player resolving that card ability places that status card on their identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card ability triggers from a game function that “you” perform (such as “after you attack and defeat an enemy”), the player resolving that card ability must resolve that card ability as if the identity they control performed that game function, if able.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Exception: For abilities that trigger “after [enemy] attacks you,” “you” refers to the attacked player, even if that player defended with an ally.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a game step or card ability discards cards from “your” hand, the player resolving that game step or card ability discards the cards from their hand.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card ability searches “your” deck, the player resolving that ability searches for cards in their deck.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a game step or card ability performs a game function against a non-identity card “you” control (such as exhausting, discarding, setting aside, etc.), the player resolving that game step or card ability performs that game function against the card in their play area.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: If a card ability triggers from a game function that “you” perform and cannot be interpreted in such a way that would refer to the resolving player’s identity (such as “after you discard cards from your hand”), the player resolving that card ability must personally resolve and perform the game function(s) of that ability.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Events — Attacks, thwarts, defenses, action abilities, and triggered abilities that resolve from a player playing an event are also considered to be performed by that player’s identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Resources — Attacks, thwarts, defenses, and triggered abilities that resolve from a player spending a resource card are also considered to be performed by that player’s identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Upgrades — Unless attached to a different friendly character, upgrade cards are considered to be an extension of the controlling player’s identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Allies — Attacks, thwarts, defenses, action abilities, and triggered abilities that resolve from allies in play under a player’s control are not considered to be performed by that player’s identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Encounter cards — Triggered abilities that resolve from encounter cards are not considered to be performed by that player’s identity, whether those abilities are optional or forced.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Player Side Schemes — Triggered abilities that resolve from player side schemes in play under a player’s control are not considered to be performed by that player’s identity.

entries.title: YOU, YOUR
entries.fragment: Supports — Attacks, thwarts, defenses, action abilities, and triggered abilities that resolve from supports in play under a player’s control are not considered to be performed by that player’s identity.
